how: A9 becomes O17 TURN_L (pin 6) - A10 becomes O18 TURN_R (pin 33) - A11 becomes O19 REVERSE (pin 20) - A12 becomes O20 INTERIOR (pin 34; it is the dash illumination bus now, the name stays) - A13 becomes O21 START_RLY (pin 21) - A14 becomes O22 KEEP_ALIVE (pin 8).
expect: Six 7 A outputs named, all disabled

how: A1 TURN_STALK (pin 29) - A2 WIPER_STALK (pin 16) - A3 BRAKE_PARK (pin 30) - A4 POPUP_L (pin 17; it reads the gear lever's Park/Neutral contact now) - A5 POPUP_R (pin 31; the lever's Reverse contact) - A6 DOOR_PINS (pin 18) - A7 OIL_PRESS (pin 32) - A8 HAZ_HORN_WINK (pin 19) - A15 HEADLIGHT_SW (pin 35) - A16 KEY_POS (pin 22). The ladders that switch to ground (A1-A6, A8) need the input's own pull-up to +5 V switched on (the PMU's selectable 10 kOhm, PMU manual p.28 and p.71), so that an open wire reads over 990. The record does not spell out the pull-up or pull-down setting for A7, A15 and A16: use the client's default, note what it is, and say so in the app - confirm.
expect: Ten inputs named

do: Create each ladder's states, without windows
how: A1: LEFT, RIGHT, OFF. A2: WASH, HIGH, LOW, INT, OFF. A3: IDLE, PARKED, BRAKE, BRAKE+PARKED. A4: IDLE, CRANK_OK. A5: IDLE, REVERSE. A6: CLOSED, DRV, PASS, BOTH. A8: IDLE, WINK_R, WINK_L, HORN, HAZARD, HAZ+HORN. A15: OFF, PARK, HEAD_LO, HEAD_HI, PASS. A16: OFF, ACC, RUN, START. How each is told apart: A1, A2, A6, A8 on plain windows; A3, A4, A5 on upward windows (each state runs from its reading minus the window up to the next state's lower edge); A15 and A16 on conductance (next step). Leave every window number empty.
expect: Every state exists by name; no numbers yet

how: A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A8: under 50 counts is a short, over 990 is an open - both a FAULT. A7: under 20 is a short, a sender fault and never oil pressure; over 1000 is an open and means ZERO oil pressure, not a fault. A15 and A16: 0 is disconnected, and a reading more than 12 counts below the live OFF reading is a FAULT too (the switch's feed is dead).
expect: Each input has its fault thresholds

do: Build the conductance decode for A15 and A16
how: Function for each: g = (k1 x v - k2) / (V - v), where v is the input in volts and V is the PMU's own supply reading. Start with k1 = 0.110 and k2 = 0.050; k2 is refitted at E26. States by g: OFF 0 - ACC and PARK 0.030 - RUN and HEAD_LO 0.097 - HEAD_HI 0.219 - START 0.244 (0.214 if ACC drops out in START) - PASS 0.522. Boundaries between them: 0.015, 0.055, 0.150, and 0.340 on A15. If CK15 found the client cannot divide: build the 2-D table of input volts against supply volts instead; if it cannot do that either, fixed windows sized over 11.5-14.8 V (A16 RUN 1153-1470 counts, START above 1490).
expect: A15 and A16 each give a named state from g
caution: Fixed windows only hold while the key sees 10.4 V or more during cranking. CK14 checks that at the first start.

how: HEAD_LOW: on when A15 is HEAD_LO. HEAD_HIGH: on when A15 is HEAD_HI or PASS. TAIL_PARK: on when A15 is PARK or higher; hold the previous state while PASS is active. BRAKE: on when A3 is BRAKE or BRAKE+PARKED. REVERSE: on when A5 is REVERSE and A16 is RUN or higher. INTERIOR (O20, the dash illumination): on when A15 is PARK or higher, as TAIL_PARK, PWM at the dimmer's duty; the dimmer's duty comes from the control panel; never from a door. On every one of these: while its input reads FAULT, hold the last state and raise the warning (LIGHT SWITCH FAULT for A15).
expect: Six lamp outputs have logic

do: Enter the flasher, the turn signals and the horn
how: Flasher: 1.5 Hz, 50 % duty, made in the PMU. hazard is true when A8 is HAZARD or HAZ+HORN; it overrides the stalk and works with the key out. TURN_L: ((A16 is RUN or higher and A1 is LEFT) or hazard) and flasher phase. TURN_R: ((A16 is RUN or higher and A1 is RIGHT) or hazard) and flasher phase - the stalk needs the key in RUN, the hazards never do (D-538). HORN: A8 is HORN or HAZ+HORN.
expect: TURN_L, TURN_R and HORN have logic

do: Enter the wipers and the washer
how: WIPE_LOW, with braking ON: A16 is ACC or higher, and (A2 is LOW, or A2 is WASH, or (A2 is INT and the interval timer), or (wiper latch and A3 not PARKED)). WIPE_HIGH: A16 is ACC or higher and A2 is HIGH. Nothing wipes with the key out (D-538). Park: when the stalk goes to OFF with the wipers running, hold O8 until A3 reads PARKED or BRAKE+PARKED, then release. Intermittent: a 3 s pause between full sweeps, each sweep runs until PARKED. One-touch: LOW held under 400 ms gives one sweep to PARKED. Washer: WASH holds O8 on; after release keep O8 on for two more sweeps. The washer pump itself is relay K12, closed by the stalk contact, not by the PMU.
expect: WIPE_LOW and WIPE_HIGH have logic

do: Enter the pop-up cycle and the motor bus
how: MOTOR_BUS (O1): popup_cycle or window_req. popup_cycle starts when A15 enters HEAD, or leaves HEAD, or A8 is WINK_L or WINK_R with A16 at ACC or lower. It keeps O1 on until O1's current has sat at the bus's idle for 300 ms, and at least 300 ms after the start. 4 s above idle is an obstruction: O1 off, fault flag. A wink with the lights off also raises O2 for the moment. Refuse a new pop-up command while window_req is true or O1 reads above 20 A. window_req is any of the four window keys held in frame 0x400; refuse it, do not queue it, while popup_cycle is true. Leave the idle threshold empty: it is entered at MG15.
expect: O1 has its logic; the idle threshold is still empty

do: Enter ignition, fuel pump and start
how: IGNITION (O12): on when A16 is RUN or higher; off only after A16 has read a clean OFF or ACC for 200 ms; while A16 reads FAULT it holds its last state as long as oil_ok is true, never turns on from a FAULT, and shows KEY FAULT. FUEL_PUMP (O5): A16 is START, or (ignition on and a 3 s prime timer running from ignition on), or (ignition on and oil_ok). oil_ok latches when A7 is BELOW the OIL_MIN count (pressure pulls the reading down) and clears after 5 s of A7 at or above OIL_MIN, or when ignition goes off. An open reading (over 1000) is zero pressure; a short (under 20) can never latch oil_ok. No CAN value in this gate, ever. Leave OIL_MIN empty. START_RLY (O21): A16 is START and A4 is CRANK_OK; release when A16 leaves START.
expect: O12, O5 and O21 have logic; OIL_MIN is empty

do: Enter accessory, keep-alive, comfort, blower and defog
how: ACCESSORY (O10): A16 is ACC or higher, or release_pulse, or (ignition on and oil_ok). release_pulse is short and self-clearing, raised only by the hatch or fuel-door key from frame 0x400. KEEP_ALIVE (O22): on at any wake; off 30 s after the last input change with A16 OFF, A6 CLOSED and A8 IDLE; forced off after 30 min with A16 OFF whatever A6 reads - except while hazard is true, which holds the car awake with no limit; the 30 min timer restarts when the hazards go off. If CK06 found the Delayed turn off panel reaches 30 minutes, use the panel for this. COMFORT (O15): A16 is RUN or higher. BLOWER (O16): A16 is RUN or higher, a steady feed - enter it and leave the output DISABLED. DEFOG (O4): A16 is ACC or higher and the panel's defog key; the A16 part is read from the ladder, never from the bus.
expect: O10, O22, O15, O16 and O4 have logic

how: Warn below 12.0 V. Shed COMFORT, INTERIOR, ACCESSORY and DEFOG only after about 10 s continuously below 11.5 V, never while A16 is START, and restore them only once the supply is back above about 12.0 V. ACCESSORY (O10) and INTERIOR (O20) are never shed while the engine runs (ignition on and oil_ok). Warn above 15.0 V.
expect: Shed and warn functions exist

how: Lamp class - 3 retries, 5 s apart, then latch and raise a warning: HEAD_LOW, HEAD_HIGH, TAIL_PARK, BRAKE, TURN_L, TURN_R, REVERSE, INTERIOR, ACCESSORY, HORN, COMFORT. Motor class - 5 retries, 15 s apart, no latch: WIPE_LOW, WIPE_HIGH, BLOWER, DEFOG. Critical class - 1 retry after 2 s, then off until the key leaves RUN: FUEL_PUMP, IGNITION, START_RLY. MOTOR_BUS is conditional: 1 retry then off and flag during a pop-up cycle; 5 at 15 s with no latch during a window command only; the pop-up rule wins when both are true. No retry: KEEP_ALIVE, LS_ECU, LS_FAN.
expect: Every output has a Retry count and Retry every value
caution: A stop lamp or headlamp must never latch off silently: the warning is part of the setting.

do: Build the four frames the PMU sends on CAN2
how: 0x100 Vehicle state, 20 Hz: byte 0 key (0 OFF, 1 ACC, 2 RUN, 3 START, 4 FAULT) - byte 1 wake source bits (b0 ACC, b1 RUN, b2 door, b3 horn/hazard/wink, b4 self-hold, b5 brake, b6 DCU request) - byte 2 fault bits (b0 soft-fuse trip, b1 undervolt, b2 overvolt, b3 overtemp) - byte 3 headlights (0 OFF, 1 PARK, 2 HEAD) - byte 4 turn (0 off, 1 left, 2 right, 3 hazard) - byte 5 pop-ups (0 down, 1 raising, 2 up, 3 lowering, 4 fault) - byte 6 input-fault bits (b0 A1, b1 A2, b2 A3, b3 A4, b4 A5, b5 A6, b6 A8, b7 A15) - byte 7 a rolling counter. 0x110 Power, 10 Hz: bytes 0-1 battery mV - bytes 2-3 total current in 0.1 A - byte 4 charging (1 when the PMU's own voltage reading is above 13.2 V) - byte 7 counter. 0x120 Outputs, 5 Hz: bytes 2-4 one on/off bit per output - byte 5 the channel index of the trip report - byte 6 its status (0 ok, 1 tripped, 2 retrying) - byte 7 counter. 0x130 Per-channel current, 5 Hz, one channel per frame in turn: byte 0 channel index - bytes 1-2 current in 0.01 A - bytes 3-4 soft-fuse setpoint in 0.01 A - byte 5 status (0 off, 1 on, 2 tripped, 3 retrying) - byte 7 counter.
expect: Four export frames defined
caution: 0x130's one-channel-per-frame form is what F-009 has just tried. If the client refused it, enter the fixed frames F-009 saved, and the same for a bitfield byte or the counter.

do: Enter the frames the PMU reads on CAN2
how: 0x400 Panel keys, sent by the climate unit on change plus twice a second: byte 0 b0 rear defog, b1 hatch release, b2 fuel-door release, b5 window driver up, b6 window driver down, b7 window passenger up; byte 1 b0 window passenger down. Timeout 1000 ms; on timeout every key reads released. Logged only, nothing acts on them: 0x180 (29-bit, the wideband's air-fuel frame, timeout 500 ms), 0x218 and 0x220 (timeout 3000 ms, log a received-channel fault). Enter timeouts as fractions of a second where CK13 found the client accepts them.
expect: panel_defog, the two release keys and the four window keys exist as CAN inputs

do: Add the stuck-on warning for the five safety outputs
how: For each of O2, O3, O5, O7 and O12: a function that is true when the output's measured voltage is at battery level while the output is commanded off. It raises a warning only; it switches nothing. The PMU has no status of its own for a shorted switch.
expect: Five warning functions exist

do: Save as RevA-01 and check nothing is enabled
how: Save the configuration to the PMU and to the laptop under the name RevA-01. Read the outputs list once more. Copy the file somewhere it can come back to the project.
expect: RevA-01 saved in both places; every output disabled; no limit entered

do: Open the disconnect and plug L3 into the dash post
how: Pull the wake jumper's fuse and F22 (DCU-CONST) first; the jumper itself stays on until the last step. Five plugs: L3-P (DTP 2-way), L3-M (DT 2-way), L3-S1 (DT 12-way), L3-S2 (DT 12-way), L3-S3 (DT 8-way). Match the code on the plug to the code on the receptacle. Push each until the latch clicks, then tug.
expect: Five latches clicked; no plug pulls off
caution: Two 12-way plugs fit each other's receptacles. Read the code, do not go by reach.

do: Move the column and pedal switches onto L3, each in the plug it needs
how:
Disconnect OPEN. One switch at a time, so no two leads are mixed up: where the switch keeps its factory plug, cut the harness half off the old harness with 150 mm of lead, splice each lead to the leg's wire for that terminal with a sealed butt splice - stagger the splices, sleeve the bundle - and plug the switch back in. A switch that is new takes the connector its line names. Each one:
DV18 Ignition switch ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: Not picked (01-electrical P086, not carted), so its plug cannot be known until it is. The factory switch is on X-08, drawn as two 2-way connectors (WR, BW and BY, L), with the start lead on X-09 (BY, through the 0.5 sq fusible link) - confirm
DV19 Light switch keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector E-01 in two parts on the diagram: a 2-way (R, WG) and a 6-way (RW, R, GL over RL, RY, RG); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV20 Turn stalk keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector F-02, an 8-cavity housing with 6 wires on the diagram (WG, GW, GY, GR over two not used, GO, GB), shared with the hazard switch DV21; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV21 Hazard switch keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: No plug of its own: the hazard section shares factory connector F-02 with the turn stalk DV20 (8 cavities, 6 wires on the diagram); which cavities are the hazard contact's is read off the diagram, not the car - confirm
DV22 Wiper stalk keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector D-03, 6 wires on the diagram (B, LO, LY over LR, LG, LW); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV23 Horn pad keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: No plug of its own on the diagram: the horn contact leaves the column as the GL cavity of the E-01 6-way connector (DV19) and returns through the column; how the pad itself connects at the wheel: not known - confirm
DV24 Wink switches ends in one of our own Deutsch pairs. Its plug: Board-mount switches soldered to the left plate's board (01-electrical P204, part not chosen): no plug of their own. Their three lines and the commons leave the plate on J2, a Deutsch DT13-06PA on the unit with a DT06-6S plug on the lead (D-521); that housing, DP-CUR-B, is not yet a row of housings - confirm
DV25 Brake pedal switch ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: Not picked (01-electrical P085, any 2-terminal type, Standard SLS-52 class, not carted), so its plug cannot be known until it is. The factory switch F-11 has a 2-way connector, 2 wires on the diagram (GW, W) - confirm
 Then check every end, by the labels: ignition switch (the new electrical portion) - B from L3-S2 2; ACC through 33 kOhm and IG through 15 kOhm and ST through 6.8 kOhm all onto L3-S1 1; ACC direct to L3-S1 12; IG direct to L3-S2 1. Light switch - common from F24; PARK 33 kOhm, HEAD 15 kOhm, dimmer HIGH 8.2 kOhm, PASS 3.3 kOhm onto L3-S1 2. Turn stalk - LEFT 1.8 kOhm, RIGHT 10 kOhm, OFF 47 kOhm onto L3-S1 3. Hazard - 4.7 kOhm onto L3-S1 6, with a 47 kOhm baseline to column ground. Wiper stalk - HIGH 4.7 kOhm, LOW 10 kOhm, INT 18 kOhm, OFF 47 kOhm and the WASH leg onto L3-S1 4; the WASH contact also direct to L3-S2 9. Horn pad - 8.2 kOhm onto L3-S1 11. Left plate, 4-way header J2 - pin 1 to L3-S1 9, pin 2 to L3-S1 10, pin 3 to L3-S1 11, pin 4 to dash ground.
expect: Every switch end is connected and labelled

how: Binnacle: the 6-way tail DP-ICU-A and the 12-way tail DP-ICU-B into the two receptacles in the unit's rear wall, behind the display. Click, tug.
expect: Both in. The display stays dark: its logic feed is O10, still disabled

how: Centre-stack opening: take the dust caps off the 6-way tail DP-DCU and the 12-way tail DP-DCU-B and plug them into the unit's rear wall. The left plate's 12-way cable goes into DP-DCU-E, in the upper row, if the plate is fitted: this row names only the first two. DP-DCU-C waits for E38 and DP-DCU-D for E39.
expect: Both plugs in
caution: DP-DCU-B and the two upper-row plugs are all 12-way. Read the codes.

do: Close the disconnect and reconnect the client
how: Master disconnect ON, the wake jumper's fuse back in, F22 still out. Client on DP-DIAG. Confirm every output is still disabled.
expect: PMU awake; outputs off; the Control Unit still dark

do: First 12 V on the Control Unit
how: Meter on DC volts from the node receptacle pin L4-M 9 to the ground bus (the L4 leg is not plugged in, so the pin is bare at the post). Fit F22 (3 A) and watch the unit and the meter. In the client the panel-key inputs stop timing out: frame 0x400 arrives twice a second and 0x300 five times a second.
expect: The unit's screen and lights come up; F22 intact; nothing warm; 0 V on L4-M 9 throughout
caution: If F22 blows, do not fit a bigger one: unplug DP-DCU and raise a note.

do: Prove every command stays off through power-up and reset
how: One point at a time, meter on DC volts to the ground bus, min/max hold if it has it: node receptacle pins L4-M 9, 10, 11 and 12 (the four window commands), L4-P 4 (the mirror-heat feed) and wake-strip screw 7 (the wake request). At each point pull F22, wait for the unit to go dark, refit it, three times.
expect: 0 V at all six points at every moment - no flicker on min/max
caution: Any voltage here would move a window or wake the car by itself: stop and raise a note naming the point.

do: Drive each command from its key
how: Key at ACC. Hold each window switch on the panel in turn and read L4-M 9 (driver up), 10 (driver down), 11 (passenger up), 12 (passenger down); try up and down of one side together. Press the rear-defog key, then the mirror-defog key, and read L4-P 4: note which of the two raises it.
expect: About 12 V on one pin per command and only while held; never both pins of one side; L4-P 4 follows a defog key
caution: These are bare pins at the post: one probe, a steady hand, nothing bridging two pins.

do: CK12 in the car: the wake request and the A8 wake stage
how: Key out; pull the wake jumper's fuse: the PMU switches off, its LED dark. Meter on DC volts on the A8 line at the perfboard's lead to PMU pin 19: read it at rest. Then, one at a time, watching the PMU's LED: press a panel key (the Control Unit raises wake-strip screw 7); press the horn pad; switch the hazards on and off; hold each wink button.
expect: At rest about 0.166 x the battery voltage on the line (1.99 V at 12.0 V) and the PMU stays off. Each press lights the PMU's LED for about a second and it goes dark again - the keep-alive that would hold it is O22, not enabled until MG02. No horn, no lamp: outputs are disabled
caution: A press that does not wake it is a fault in that stage or its switch end: find it now, the perfboard is still in reach.

do: Read the Control Unit's sleeping current on F22
how: Still asleep, a minute after the last press. Pull F22 and bridge its holder with the meter on the 10 A range, a probe tip on each contact; when the reading is small and steady, drop to mA. Write it down, take the probes out, refit F22, and put the wake jumper's fuse back for the readings that follow.
expect: About 10 mA - confirm; what it is goes in the note
caution: 10 A range first: the unit wakes as the meter connects.

do: Read the key: OFF first, then fit k2
how: Key out; the wake jumper keeps the PMU awake for this reading, and it sits on the brake-wake screw, clear of the key's own wires. Read A16 in volts. Set k2 = 0.110 x that reading, so that g reads 0 at OFF. Note the raw OFF count too.
expect: g = 0 at OFF

do: Read the key at ACC, RUN and START
how: Turn to ACC, RUN, then hold START for a few seconds. Nothing cranks: the new switch feeds only the PMU and O21 is disabled. Write each live reading into the client. Expected g: ACC 0.030, RUN 0.097, START 0.244 (0.214 if ACC drops out in START). Boundaries 0.015, 0.055, 0.150.
expect: OFF, ACC, RUN, START each decode by name, each well inside its band
caution: A START value near a boundary matters: it is the reading that cranks the engine. Fix the resistor, not the boundary.

do: Read the light switch: OFF first, then every position
how: Light switch OFF: read A15, set its k2 the same way. Then PARK, HEAD with the dimmer low, HEAD with the dimmer high, and the stalk pulled to PASS. Expected g: PARK 0.030, HEAD_LO 0.097, HEAD_HI 0.219, PASS 0.522. Boundaries 0.015, 0.055, 0.150, 0.340. Try PASS from OFF as well as from HEAD.
expect: OFF, PARK, HEAD_LO, HEAD_HI, PASS each decode by name
caution: If PASS from OFF reads as HEAD_LO, the switch has no separate pass contact (CK17 checked for this). Stop and note it.

do: Prove a dead feed reads as a fault
how: Key at ACC: pull F3 (5 A, block A position 2 at the node). A16 must read FAULT, not OFF. Refit F3. Light switch at PARK: pull F24 (3 A inline, behind the lower dash panel). A15 must read FAULT. Refit F24.
expect: FAULT both times; normal again with the fuses back

how: A1, in counts: OFF (47 kOhm), LEFT (1.8 kOhm), RIGHT (10 kOhm). Write each live reading in. Window: reading plus and minus 55.
expect: Three separate windows; nothing under 50 or over 990

how: A2: OFF (47 kOhm), INT (18 kOhm), LOW (10 kOhm), HIGH (4.7 kOhm), and WASH held. Write each in. Window plus and minus 45. The washer relay K12 does not click today: its coil feed is O10, still disabled.
expect: Five separate windows

do: Read hazard, horn and both winks
how: A8: IDLE (47 kOhm baseline), HAZARD on (4.7 kOhm), HORN pressed (8.2 kOhm), HAZARD and HORN together, WINK_L held (18 kOhm), WINK_R held (33 kOhm). Write each in. Window plus and minus 35. The horn stays silent and the lamps stay still: outputs are disabled.
expect: Six separate windows

do: Enter the tables and check for overlap
how: For A1, A2 and A8 enter each state as its reading plus and minus the half-width. Look down each table: no two windows may touch. Work every switch once more and watch the state name change cleanly.
expect: Every position shows its own state name; nothing reads FAULT

how: Max Current for each output, in amps: O1 25.0 - O2 13.0 - O3 13.0 - O4 25.0 - O5 4.0 - O6 7.5 - O7 11 - O8 13.0 - O9 13.0 - O10 13.0 - O11 13.0 - O12 25.0 - O16 25.0 - O17 4.5 - O18 4.5 - O19 7.0 - O20 7.0 - O21 7.0 - O22 7.0. O15 has no enable-at figure in the record: leave it at the client's default and note it. O13 and O14 stay disabled with nothing entered.
expect: Nineteen limits entered

how: Inrush Current is the multiple times the expected running current; Inrush Time in ms. O1 7 x 9.5 A for 400 - O2 3 x 7.4 A for 200 - O3 3 x 8.9 A for 200 - O4 1.3 x 11.5 A for 2000 - O5 3 x 2.0 A for 150 - O6 10 x 4.4 A for 100 - O7 10 x 3.9 A for 100 - O8 7 x 4.0 A for 300 - O9 7 x 5.5 A for 300 - O10 2 x 10.0 A for 100 - O11 3 x 6.0 A for 80 - O12 2 x 10 A for 100 - O15 2 x for 200 - O16 8 x 15.0 A for 600 - O17 10 x 4.2 A for 100 - O18 10 x 4.2 A for 100 - O19 10 x 3.9 A for 100 - O20 10 x 1.5 A for 100 - O21 2 x 0.2 A for 50 - O22 2 x 0.2 A, time 0.
expect: Every lamp output has its inrush window before it is ever enabled
caution: A cold filament pulls about ten times its running current for a moment. Without the window the turn signals trip on every flash.

do: Save a new revision, take the wake jumper off, leave everything disabled
how: Save to the PMU and the laptop as the next revision after RevA-01. Read the outputs list: nothing enabled. Then pull the wake jumper's fuse, unscrew the jumper from the busbar and from wake-strip screw 6, and put it away: from here the key at ACC wakes the car, and with the key out the PMU is off until O22 is enabled at MG02.
expect: New revision saved; outputs off; the jumper gone and both screws tight again

do: Open the disconnect and lay the three legs out along the car
how: Each leg came off the bench bagged and tagged (E21-E23). Lay L2 toward the nose, L4 toward the rear, L1 toward the engine bay. Plug nothing in yet.
expect: Three legs, every end labelled

how: From the dash post out through the cowl grommet and along the inner wing to the nose splice. Then the branches: across the radiator support to each headlight bucket and pop-up motor; to both front combo lamps, both side markers and both horns; back along the cowl to the wiper motor and washer pump. The outside-air sensor's 2-way receptacle L2-OAT sits ahead of the radiator, dust-capped. Keep the 6-way signal bundle apart from the 4-way power bundle.
expect: Every L2 end reaches its device with slack and no strain
caution: Keep clear of the pop-up linkages and the fan. A pop-up moves fast when it moves.

do: Land the L2 grounds on the front star
how: The front star stud is on the radiator support. Rings on it: each headlight (14 AWG black), each pop-up bucket strap (14 AWG), each front combo lamp and side marker (16 AWG), the wiper motor (14 AWG), the washer pump (16 AWG), the wiper-park 47 kOhm baseline (16 AWG). Each horn has its own 14 AWG ring under its mounting bolt. Torque the stud to the figure written at D1 (confirm); cavity wax over it.
expect: Continuity from every device ground to the star stud

do: Route the L4 trunk through the tunnel
how: From the dash post down the tunnel to the rear node in the cargo bin, beside the 2 AWG feed and the two 1/0 cables already there. In the tunnel a branch drops to the transmission: the road-speed sensor's pair (leave its 18 in service loop) and the kick-down solenoid wire.
expect: Trunk at the rear node; transmission branch at the speedo-drive boss

how: From the rear node: along the quarter on each side to the tail lamps, licence lamps and rear markers; under the floor to the fuel pump and the tank sender; through the hatch hinge loop to the hatch-release solenoid, the luggage lamp and the defog grid - set the slack with the hatch fully open; up the C-pillar to the interior lamp; behind the driver-side quarter trim to the fuel-door solenoid. Grounds to the rear star stud in the cargo bin: the pump's own 12 AWG, the defog grid's 12 AWG, the rest 16 AWG.
expect: Every L4 end reaches its device; the hatch opens fully without pulling the loop
caution: Under the car: stands, chocks, no sparks near the tank.

do: Fit the sill node and route the sill run
how: The sill node panel goes behind the driver kick panel. Its ground stud to the chassis on 10 AWG black: bare metal, star washer, wax. The sill run comes from the dash post along the driver sill. At the sill the door-switch line (L4-S 2) splices to both new jamb switches: driver through 24 kOhm and a 1N4148, passenger through 8.2 kOhm and a 1N4148, with a 47 kOhm baseline from the splice to sill ground. The interior lamp's RY wire reaches each switch through its own 1N4007.
expect: Sill node fixed; D1 and D2 receptacles pinned and their door plugs sealed; relay sockets K5-K8 wired

do: Route L1 into the engine bay
how: From the dash post through the firewall grommet on the passenger side to the junction in the bay. Branches: along the upper rear housing to the two coils and two igniters; down the front of the block to the alternator plug; to the water-temperature and oil-pressure senders at the rear housing, one below the other; under the intake to the starter, K9 and the inhibitor switch on the transmission; along the firewall to the brake-fluid switch on the reservoir. The shielded tach wire crosses every ignition lead at 90 degrees and stays 50 mm from them.
expect: Every L1 end reaches its device
caution: Keep the leg off the exhaust and clear of the belt and fan.

how: P-clip each run to the body (the backbone was clipped every 12 in at E10; the legs' spacing is not in the record). A grommet at every hole a bundle passes through. A drip loop before every node. A turn of cloth tape every 150 mm. Do not final-wrap anything.
expect: Nothing hangs, nothing rubs on an edge

do: Fit F17 and wire the start relay K9
how: Disconnect OPEN. F17: fit the 30 A MIDI fuse in its holder beside the starter's main stud; the holder's input is on the stud. K9 in its weatherproof socket on the inner fender: terminal 30 from F17 on 10 AWG red; terminal 87 to the starter's small S terminal on 10 AWG red - leave the S end unconnected and insulated until MG23, the factory wire is still on it; terminal 86 is the L1-S1 1 wire; terminal 85 to a ring on the engine block, 16 AWG black.
expect: K9 wired; its 87 lead capped beside the starter
caution: The starter's main stud is on the 250 A fuse and is live whenever the disconnect is closed. Disconnect open, and check 0 V on the stud before a spanner touches it.

do: Plug the three legs into the dash post
how: L2: L2-P (DTP 4-way), L2-M (DT 8-way), L2-S (DT 6-way). L4: L4-P (DTP 4-way), L4-M (DT 12-way), L4-S (DT 8-way), L4-S2 (DT 8-way). L1: L1-P (DTP 4-way), L1-S1 (DT 12-way), L1-S2 (DT 12-way). Match the code on both halves, push to the click, tug.
expect: Ten plugs latched
caution: L1-S1, L1-S2 and L4-M are all 12-way, and L2-M, L4-S and L4-S2 are all 8-way. Read the codes.

do: Leave every device end unjoined and insulated
how: Loads stay on the factory harness until their own row in E28. Fold each new device end back beside its device, cover any bare terminal, and leave its label showing.
expect: No new wire touches a device or the body

do: Close the disconnect and reconnect the client
how: Disconnect ON, key to ACC - the wake jumper went at E26, so the key wakes the PMU now - client on DP-DIAG. Confirm every output is still disabled.
expect: PMU visible; outputs off

do: Read the brake pedal and wiper park input, A3
how: IDLE with the pedal up; BRAKE with the pedal pressed. PARKED and BRAKE+PARKED need the wiper motor's park contact on the new leg: if the motor is still on the factory harness read these two at MG05. Write each live reading in. Upward decode, half-width 30.
expect: IDLE and BRAKE named correctly

do: Read the gear lever inputs, A4 and A5
how: A4: CRANK_OK with the lever in P and again in N; IDLE in every other position. A5: REVERSE with the lever in R; IDLE elsewhere. These contacts are in the inhibitor switch on the transmission: if it is still on the factory harness, read them when it moves (MG12 for reverse, MG23 for start). Upward decode, half-width 20.
expect: P and N give CRANK_OK; R gives REVERSE; nothing else does
caution: Wheels chocked and the engine cannot start: the lever is being moved through every gear.

how: CLOSED with both doors shut; DRV with the driver door open; PASS with the passenger door open; BOTH with both open. The jamb switches are new and already on the new leg. Window plus and minus 20.
expect: Four separate windows

do: CK12 in the car: the door wake stage
how: Key out: the PMU switches off, its LED dark. Meter on DC volts on the A6 line at the perfboard's lead to PMU pin 18: read it at rest with both doors shut. Then open and shut the driver's door, then the passenger's, watching the PMU's LED. Key back to ACC afterwards. The lamp's RY wire is not on these switches until MG01: the same test is repeated there with the lamp at DOOR.
expect: At rest about 0.166 x the battery voltage on the line (1.99 V at 12.0 V) and the PMU stays off. Each door opening lights the PMU's LED for about a second, then it goes dark again - the keep-alive that would hold it is not enabled until MG02
caution: A door that does not wake it: the diode at that switch is the wrong way round or the stage is at fault. Find it now, while the sill and the perfboard are open.

do: Enter the tables and save a new revision
how: Enter each state from its reading. A7, oil pressure, is read at the first idle at the end of E28. Save as the next revision. Nothing enabled.
expect: Revision saved; outputs off

do: Set up, and learn the loop on paper before the first circuit
how: Laptop on DP-DIAG, client connected, every output still disabled. Long meter lead clipped at the dash node. Label printer loaded. For every circuit below: (1) disconnect OPEN - unplug the load, cut its harness-side plug off the old harness with 150 mm of lead, label the stub MIGRATED and today's date, tape it back; (2) splice the plug's leads to the new wires, staggered, sealed and sleeved - or fit the ring, spade or new connector the row names - and plug the load in; (3) disconnect ON - enable that one output; (4) work it and read its current in the client; (5) with it running, busbar to device + under 0.5 V and device - to ground bus under 0.3 V; (6) write the two readings down. Move to the next only when this one works.
expect: Ready; nothing enabled

do: MG01 - interior lamp, on fuse F12
how:
Factory side: the lamp in the interior mirror housing has two wires, LY (constant feed) and RY (to the door switches). Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L4-M 8, 16 AWG red, up the C-pillar to the lamp's LY terminal; it is always-hot from the busbar through F12, a 5 A sealed inline fuse at the node. The lamp's own switch does the rest: ON goes to the roof-rail ground (16 AWG black); DOOR goes to the new RY wire, which reaches both jamb switches through a 1N4007 each. Fit the 5 A fuse in F12. There is no output to enable and no current in the client: this lamp is on a fuse, not on the PMU. Then the last part of check CK12: lamp switch at DOOR, key out, the PMU off - a door opening must still light the PMU's LED for a moment, with the lamp's RY wire live on the jamb switches.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV39 Interior / spot lamp keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: H-06 on the mirror assembly: two single-way connectors on the diagram (LY, RY), read as bullet terminals in 00-CAR's terminals rows; no ground wire is drawn. Which half is on the lamp: not known - confirm
DV41 Door jamb switches ends in a heat-shrink ring or spade on the part's own stud, screw or tab. Its plug: New generic adjustable plunger pin switches (01-electrical P084, an unnamed 6-pack): no maker's sheet, so the terminal type and size are not known. The devices row gives each one terminal, the body grounding in the jamb - confirm
expect: Switch ON: lit, key out. Switch DOOR: lit with either door open, dark with both shut. Lamp + within 0.5 V of the busbar

do: MG02 and MG26 - head unit and USB-C on O10, and the head unit's memory feed through K11
how:
Factory side: the head unit is aftermarket, spliced in behind the dash by a previous owner - how is not in the record: note what you find. Free its red, yellow, orange and black wires and label what they came off. New side: L3-M 1 (14 AWG orange, from O10) to the head unit's red ACC wire and the USB-C module's +; L3-M 2 (14 AWG red, from F1, 10 A, block B) to the head unit's yellow memory wire; head unit black to dash ground on 14 AWG; USB-C - to dash ground on 16 AWG. Enable O22 KEEP_ALIVE first (7.0 A): relay K11 pulls in whenever the car is awake and feeds block B. Now item (iii) of check CK12: key out, wait until the car is asleep, then turn to ACC and time from the turn to K11's click, in seconds - the wake stages' pulse, about 0.9 s on 2.2 uF, has to outlast it; note the figure. Then enable O10 ACCESSORY (13.0 A). Key to ACC.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV28 Head unit ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: Pioneer DMH-W4660NEX (luxury LP55): the maker's installation sheet was not reached, so the unit's power connector, its ways and whether its power cord is in the box are not known. The devices row assumes a cord with red, yellow, orange, black and blue / white leads, RCA pre-outs and a microphone lead - confirm
DV29 USB-C module ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: No part is chosen (ident Aftermarket; no parts row in 01-electrical or luxury names it), so its plug cannot be known until it is picked; the devices row gives it 2 conductors (+ and -) - confirm
expect: K11 clicks; 12 V on L3-M 2; head unit on at ACC and keeps its memory; USB-C charges a phone; the instrument unit boots, its logic is on O10. O10 reads up to about 10 A with everything loaded; O22 reads about zero - it is under the PMU's measuring floor
caution: O10 also feeds the release relays' branch, the road-speed sensor and the washer relay coil. If O10 trips here, pull F33 and try again.

do: MG03 - dash illumination on O20, the display's backlight feed F16, and the soft-fuse trip test
how:
Factory side: the dash lamps for the heater panel, the gear-lever surround and the switch panel are on RL from the factory dimmer. Unplug each, label, tape back. New side: L3-S1 8 (16 AWG red, from O20) to those three lamps' RL and the head unit's orange illumination wire; lamp grounds to dash ground on 16 AWG. O20 also gives the instrument unit its dimming reference. Enable O20 INTERIOR (7.0 A). Light switch to PARK. Fit the 5 A fuse in F16: it feeds the display's backlight, but from O12, which is not enabled until MG21 - the backlight is proven then. Trip test, here on the first PMU lamp output (the interior lamp is on fuse F12 and has no soft fuse) - confirm the choice of O20: set O20's limit to 2 A, switch it on, and short the L3-S1 8 wire to ground on purpose for a moment.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV30 Dash illumination lamps keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: E-06 heater panel: 2-way connector, 2 wires on the diagram (RL, B). E-07 select lever: two single-way connectors (RL, B). E-10 switch panel: drawn as a bulb socket with 2 wires (RL, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: Dash lamps on with PARK and HEAD, dimming with the panel's dimmer; about 1.5 A. On the short: status 3 OVERCURRENT, three retries 5 s apart, then latched off with a warning. Put the limit back to 7.0 A afterwards
caution: Short it only with the limit at 2 A and only on this 16 AWG illumination wire.

how:
Factory side: each horn behind the front bumper has one GY wire from the factory horn relay. Pull the GY off each horn, label, tape back. New side: L2-M 3 (14 AWG orange, from O11) splits at the nose to each horn's terminal; each horn's case has its own 14 AWG black ring under its mounting bolt to the front star. Enable O11 HORN (13.0 A). Press the pad with the key out.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV14 Horns ends in a heat-shrink ring or spade on the part's own stud, screw or tab. Its plug: Single terminal per horn, 1 wire on the diagram (GY), labelled a single spade in 00-CAR's terminals rows; the case grounds through the bracket. Terminal size: not known - confirm
expect: Both horns sound, key out; 4 to 8 A; A8 reads HORN while pressed
caution: It is loud at arm's length. Ear protection if your head is in the nose.

do: MG05 - wipers LOW and park on O8
how:
Factory side: the wiper motor at the cowl has a 4-way plug (L, LB, LW, LR) and a single B ground. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L2-M 1 (14 AWG orange, from O8) to the motor's LW, the low brush; the park contact L through 12 kOhm to L2-S 3; LB left unconnected and capped; B to the front star on 14 AWG black. How this motor returns its current was the question of check CK09: wire it as the leg was built after that check. Enable O8 WIPE_LOW (13.0 A). Key to RUN, stalk to LOW, then OFF mid-sweep. Now read A3's PARKED and BRAKE+PARKED states and enter them.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV15 Wiper motor keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector D-02, 4 wires on the diagram (LW, LR over L, LB), plus a separate single-way connector for B; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: Wipers run at low speed, about 4 A; at OFF they carry on to the bottom and stop there; A3 reads PARKED at rest
caution: Arms and linkage move at once. Wet the glass or lift the arms off it.

how: New side: L2-M 2 (14 AWG orange, from O9) to the motor's LR, the high brush. Enable O9 WIPE_HIGH (13.0 A). Stalk to HIGH, then OFF; then INT; then a quick flick to LOW and back.
expect: High speed about 5.5 A; parks from HIGH; INT gives one sweep, a 3 s pause, another sweep; a flick under 400 ms gives one sweep

how:
Factory side: the washer pump has LB (+) and LY. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L2-M 4 (14 AWG orange, from K12 terminal 87) to the pump's LB; the pump's LY to the front star on 16 AWG black. K12's coil is fed from O10 and grounded by the stalk's WASH contact through L3-S2 9; its contact takes power from O8. Nothing new to enable. Key to RUN, hold WASH.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV16 Washer pump keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector D-01, 2 wires on the diagram (LY, LB); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: K12 clicks, the pump runs only while WASH is held, the wipers run and make two more sweeps after release. Pump 3 to 5 A
caution: The pump was not working when last checked (CK22). A silent pump with 12 V on LB while WASH is held is the pump, not the wiring.

do: MG08 - tail, park, markers and licence lamps on O6
how:
Factory side: every one of these lamps is on RG. Unplug at each lamp, label, tape back. New side, front: L2-M 7 (14 AWG orange, from O6) splits at the nose to both front combo lamps' and both front side markers' RG. Rear: L4-M 1 (14 AWG orange) splits at the hatch to both tail lamps, both licence lamps and both rear markers. Grounds to the front and rear star studs on 16 AWG black. Enable O6 TAIL_PARK (7.5 A). Light switch to PARK, then HEAD, then pull PASS.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV12 Front combo lamps keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector F-05 / F-06, 3 wires on the diagram (RG, GR or GO, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known. The LED bulbs (luxury LP53) go in the lamp's own bulb holder, so the plug does not change - confirm
DV13 Front side markers keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector F-12 / F-13, 2 wires on the diagram (B, RG); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known. The LED bulb (luxury LP53) goes in the lamp's own holder - confirm
DV37 Rear combo lamps keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector F-07 / F-08, a 6-cavity housing with 5 wires on the diagram (GR or GO, RW, one not used, over G, RG, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV38 Licence lamps + rear markers keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: F-04 licence lamps: two single-way connectors per lamp on the diagram (RG, B). F-14 / F-15 rear markers: 2-way connector, 2 wires (B, RG); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: All ten lamps lit at PARK and HEAD, steady while PASS is pulled; about 4.4 to 5.4 A

how:
Factory side: the stop filaments are on G at each rear combo lamp; the factory pedal switch has GW in and W out. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L4-M 2 (14 AWG orange, from O7) splits to both rear lamps' G. The new pedal switch through 4.7 kOhm on L3-S1 5 is the A3 input; a separate plunger on the pedal wakes the PMU through L3-S1 7. Enable O7 BRAKE (11 A). Press the pedal with the key out and the car asleep.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV25 Brake pedal switch ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: Not picked (01-electrical P085, any 2-terminal type, Standard SLS-52 class, not carted), so its plug cannot be known until it is. The factory switch F-11 has a 2-way connector, 2 wires on the diagram (GW, W) - confirm
expect: Brake lamps light with the key out; about 7 A on four 27 W filaments; A3 reads BRAKE

do: MG10 - left turn signals on O17
how: Factory side: GR at the front left combo lamp and the rear left lamp. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L2-M 5 (16 AWG red) to the front left lamp's GR; L4-M 5 (16 AWG red) to the rear left lamp's GR; both from O17, with a tap to the instrument unit for the tell-tale. Enable O17 TURN_L (4.5 A). Key to RUN, stalk LEFT.
expect: Front and rear left flash together at 1.5 Hz, about 4.2 A on bulbs; the left arrow shows on the display

do: MG11 - right turn signals on O18, then the hazards
how: Factory side: GO at the front right and rear right lamps. New side: L2-M 6 and L4-M 6 (16 AWG red, from O18). Enable O18 TURN_R (4.5 A). Stalk RIGHT. Then stalk LEFT with the hazard switch on, and hazards with the key out.
expect: Right side flashes at 1.5 Hz; the hazard switch flashes all four whatever the stalk says, key in or out

how:
Factory side: the inhibitor switch on the transmission has one 4-pin plug: GY in and RW out are the reverse pair, BY and BW the start pair. Unplugging it takes all four off the factory harness, so join all four now. At the rear lamps the reverse filaments are on RW. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: the switch's GY through 8.2 kOhm to L1-S2 7 and its RW to a block ground ring on 16 AWG black, with a 47 kOhm baseline at the switch; its BY through 8.2 kOhm to L1-S1 11 and its BW to a block ground ring, with its own 47 kOhm baseline; L4-M 7 (16 AWG red, from O19) splits to both rear lamps' RW. Read A5 now if E27 could not: REVERSE in R, IDLE elsewhere. Enable O19 REVERSE (7.0 A). Key to RUN, lever to R.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV05 Inhibitor switch keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector A-06, 4 wires on the diagram (BY, GY over BW, RW); whether the switch carries a lead of its own, housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: Both reverse lamps lit only in R with the key at RUN; about 3.9 A
caution: Wheels chocked, foot on the brake. The starter cannot run, but the lever is in R.

do: MG13 - headlight low beam on O2
how:
Factory side: each headlamp plug has RY, RL and B. Unplug both, label, tape back. New side: L2-P 1 (12 AWG red, from O2) splits at the nose into a 14 AWG branch to each lamp plug's RY; each lamp's B to the front star on 14 AWG black. RY as low beam is the car's own record and was checked at CK23 - if low and high come out swapped, swap L2-P 1 and L2-P 2's branches at the nose splice and note it. Enable O2 HEAD_LOW (13.0 A). Light switch to HEAD, dimmer low. The pop-ups do not rise yet: O1 is still disabled.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV10 Headlights ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: The Grote 94401-5 LED unit (luxury LP41) has an H4 connection, 3-pin by Grote's family sheet, and comes with an adapter block for 2E1-style harnesses. The factory lamp connector E-08 / E-09 has 3 wires on the diagram (RL, RY, B); whether that socket mates the H4 connection: not known - confirm
expect: Both low beams lit; halogen would read 7.4 A, the LED housings in the car far less; lamp + within 0.5 V of the busbar

do: MG14 - headlight high beam on O3
how: New side: L2-P 2 (12 AWG red, from O3) splits at the nose into a 14 AWG branch to each lamp plug's RL; a tap on O3 goes to the instrument unit for the high-beam tell-tale. Enable O3 HEAD_HIGH (13.0 A). Dimmer high; then PASS from OFF.
expect: Both high beams lit on dimmer high and while PASS is pulled; the high-beam tell-tale shows on the display; halogen would read 8.9 A

do: MG15 and MG16 - both pop-up motors on O1, in one session
how:
Factory side: each motor has a 4-wire plug: WR, R, RY, YG. Unplug both, label, tape back. New side: L2-P 3 (12 AWG red, from O1) splits at the nose to both motors' WR, the motor feed. Left motor: R (up) from L2-S 1, RY (down) from L2-P 4. Right motor: R from L2-S 2, RY from L2-S 6. All four are 14 AWG red, from relays K1 and K2 at the node through F37 (5 A). YG is capped at each motor. Each bucket has a 14 AWG black strap to the front star. Fit F37. Enter the pop-up cycle's idle threshold from the two currents read at CK08's powered test. Enable O1 MOTOR_BUS (25.0 A). Light switch to HEAD, then OFF. Then each wink button alone with the key out. Then check CK16: log O1 current and popup_cycle in the client at the fastest rate, meter on min/max between the front star stud and the dash ground bus; lights on and off three times, hold a wink, press a window key on the panel during a transit. CK16's method says engine idling: repeat it after MG23 - confirm.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV11 Pop-up motors keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector E-03 / E-04, 4 wires on the diagram (YG, WR, RY, R), drawn as four round terminals in a cross; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: Both lamps rise on HEAD and drop on OFF, each stopping itself; a wink moves one lamp only. Each cycle: O1 above idle within 300 ms, back to idle after about a second, popup_cycle clear within 300 ms and never near 4 s. The window key during a transit is refused. Front-star offset under 0.28 V
caution: Hands, tools and leads out of both buckets before O1 is enabled. A stalled motor pulls 15 to 25 A: if a lamp jams, switch off - do not help it by hand.

how:
Factory side: the blower motor and resistor pack plug (LO feed from the 20 A blower fuse). The motor is dead. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: nothing is connected. L3-BLW, a DTP 2-way receptacle at the heater case, stays dust-capped: cavity 1 is the feed from O16 (12 AWG red), cavity 2 the return to dash ground (12 AWG black). O16 BLOWER stays DISABLED this build. Check cavity 2 to the dash ground bus with the meter.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV27 Blower motor ends in one of our own Deutsch pairs. Its plug: New motor, Four Seasons 35483 class, 2 wires; the maker's own connector is not known (one search found no sheet). The leg ends in our Deutsch DTP04-2P receptacle and the motor's lead takes the DTP06-2S plug - confirm the motor's lead; housing L3-BLW
DV55 Blower final stage ends in one of our own Deutsch pairs. Its plug: Pololu G2 24v21 (#2995): a bare board, no plug of its own - VIN, GND, OUTA and OUTB on 5 mm-pitch holes for the two 2-way screw terminal blocks in the box (rated 16 A), logic on 0.1 in header holes. Its adapter lead is ours and is not drawn yet (confirm); it plugs into L3-BLW
expect: Continuity from L3-BLW 2 to ground; dust cap on; O16 still disabled

do: MG18 - courtesy lamps on fuse F19
how:
Factory side: the glove box lamp (LO, BL) and the luggage lamp (LY, RB). Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L3-S2 10 (16 AWG red) to the glove box lamp's +, its - through the lid switch to dash ground; L4-S 8 (16 AWG red) to the luggage lamp's +, its - through its lid switch to the rear star. Both from F19, 3 A, block A position 3, always-hot. Fit the fuse. No output to enable.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV31 Glove box lamp keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: H-01 lamp: drawn as a bulb socket with 2 wires on the diagram (LO, BL). H-02 lid switch: one single-way connector (BL) and a ring terminal (B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV40 Luggage lamp keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: H-11 lamp: two single-way connectors on the diagram (LY, RB). H-12 lid switch: one single-way connector (RB), closing to body ground; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: Each lamp lights when its lid opens, key out

do: MG27 - rear defog grid on O4
how:
Factory side: the grid's LG feed plug is at the rear pillar (1985 manual - confirm on the car); the factory dash switch is broken. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L4-P 1 (12 AWG red, from O4) to the grid's LG terminal; the grid's B to the rear star on 12 AWG black. Enable O4 DEFOG (25.0 A). Key to ACC, press the rear-defog key on the climate panel. The grid is peeling and nobody has measured it: the reading is the measurement.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV33 Rear defog grid keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: G-25: two single-way connectors on the diagram, one per side of the grid (LG, B), drawn in two different shapes; whether they are tabs on the glass, and their size: not known - confirm
expect: O4 on only with the key at ACC or higher and the panel key; 10 to 13 A expected cold on a whole grid, less with broken lines; no response to the key with the key out
caution: Do not scrape or flex the hatch glass around the grid tabs.

do: MG20 - fuel pump on O5 through relay K13, and the tank sender
how:
Factory side: the pump has BLg (+) and B; the tank sender has Y and B. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L4-P 2 (12 AWG red) to the pump's +; it comes from K13 terminal 87, and K13's terminal 30 is fed by O5. The pump's - goes on its own 12 AWG black to the rear star. Sender: L4-S 1 (16 AWG grey) to the sender's Y, the sender's B to the rear star on 16 AWG black. Enable O5 FUEL_PUMP (4.0 A). Key to RUN.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV34 Fuel pump ends in a heat-shrink ring or spade on the part's own stud, screw or tab. Its plug: Two terminals on the pump for two terminal wires; Carter's sheet draws both a screw-type and a push-on-type terminal and does not say which the P4070 has. Which pump is on the car is itself still to be read off it - confirm
DV36 Fuel level sender keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector C-01, 2 wires on the diagram (B, Y); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: K13 clicks at RUN (its coil is on the ignition switch, not the PMU); the pump runs for the 3 s prime and stops, because there is no oil pressure with the engine off; about 2 to 2.4 A while it runs
caution: Fuel: no sparks, extinguisher within reach, check for leaks at the pump before and after.

do: MG21 - ignition and alternator excitation on O12
how:
Factory side: the BW ignition feed at both coils and both igniters; the alternator's 2-way plug (BW and WB). Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L1-P 1 (12 AWG red, from O12) splits at the coil bracket to the BW of coil T, coil L, igniter T and igniter L, with the noise capacitor on that branch; L1-S1 2 (16 AWG red, through F15, 7.5 A) to the alternator plug's BW. Fit F15. Enable O12 IGNITION (25.0 A). Key to RUN. O12 also brings up F16: the display's backlight comes on now.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV01 Coils + igniters keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Igniters B-20 and B-21: factory connector, 2 wires each on the diagram (YG, BW and YL, BW). Coils B-18 and B-19: one single-way connector each (YG, YL) plus a ring terminal for BW; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV04 Alternator keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory 2-way coupler A-08 on the regulator, 2 wires on the diagram (BW, WB), plus the B output A-09 drawn as a ring terminal (WR); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: 12 V on the coils' BW at RUN, gone 200 ms after the key reaches ACC or OFF; 12 V on the alternator's BW; the display is lit
caution: The coils are live at RUN. The engine still cannot crank.

do: MG24 - kick-down circuit on fuse F21
how:
Factory side: the kick-down switch at the throttle pedal and the solenoid on the transmission, joined by a BR wire. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: L3-S2 12 (16 AWG red, through F21, 5 A, off O12) to one switch terminal; the other terminal to L3-S3 4, which is linked at the post to L4-S2 7 and runs down the tunnel to the solenoid; the solenoid's other side is its own ground on the case - prove that with the meter. Fit F21. Key to RUN, press the pedal to the floor.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV50 Kick-down switch keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: B-32: two single-way connectors on the diagram (BW, BR), one per terminal; whether bare push-on terminals or 1-way housings, and which half is on the switch: not known - confirm
DV51 Kick-down solenoid keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: B-33: one single-way connector on the diagram (BR); the return is through the transmission case. Whether a bare push-on terminal or a 1-way housing, and which half is on the solenoid: not known - confirm
expect: 12 V at the solenoid with the pedal floored, 0 V otherwise; the solenoid should click - it is believed working, not tested

do: MG22 - the meters cutover: senders, tach, charge line and road speed to the instrument unit
how:
E2's odometer reading is already in the app: it is this row's gate. Factory side: water-temperature sender (YW spade) and oil-pressure sender (BrY spade) at the rear housing; coil T negative (YG, the tach); alternator WB; brake-fluid switch (BR); parking-brake switch (BR); the speedometer cable at the transmission. Unplug each, label, tape back. The factory cluster goes dark and is not touched again. New side: YW to L1-S1 3; BrY to L1-S1 4; the shielded wire L1-S1 6 to coil T negative, shield cut back and insulated at this end; WB to L1-S2 8; fluid switch to L1-S2 1; parking-brake switch to L3-S2 11. Take the speedometer cable off and fit the pulse sensor on the transmission's speedo-drive boss: signal to L4-S 3, +12 V from L4-S 4, ground to the rear star on 16 AWG. The sensor's pulses per mile (8 000 or 16 000, by the part bought) is a setting in the instrument unit.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV06 Water temp sender ends in a heat-shrink ring or spade on the part's own stud, screw or tab. Its plug: Single terminal on the sender, 1 wire on the diagram (YW): the devices row calls it a spade, the diagram draws a single-way connector; terminal size: not known - confirm
DV07 Oil pressure sender ends in a heat-shrink ring or spade on the part's own stud, screw or tab. Its plug: Single terminal on the sender, 1 wire on the diagram (BrY): the devices row calls it a spade, the diagram draws a single-way connector; terminal size: not known - confirm
DV08 Brake fluid level switch keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector C-05, 2 wires on the diagram (BR, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV26 Parking brake switch keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory single-way connector C-04, 1 wire on the diagram (BR); the switch grounds through its body. Whether it is a bare push-on terminal or a 1-way housing, and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV47 Road-speed pulse generator ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: Not picked (01-electrical P113, Dakota Digital SEN-01-4160 / AutoMeter 5291 class, not carted, bought after M-2), so its plug cannot be known until it is; the devices row gives it 3 conductors (signal, +12 V, ground) - confirm
expect: Key at RUN: the display shows fuel level and water temperature, the brake warning with the parking brake on, and zero oil pressure with the engine stopped. The odometer starts from E2's figure - how the figure is set into the unit is the firmware's and is not in the record: note what you did
caution: Do not start this step unless F3 is done: once the factory cluster is unplugged there is no other instrument.

do: MG25 - wideband gauge on fuse F20 and CAN2
how:
The gauge controller stays in the car, hidden at the node. Factory side: wherever its power and ground are tapped today - not in the record: note what you find, label, tape back. New side: its +12 V to F20 (7.5 A, off O12); its ground to the ground bus on 16 AWG black; its AEMnet pair - cut the gauge's 2-way plug off its lead and butt-splice the pair onto the CAN2 pair at the node's splice. The sensor's own cable is never cut or extended. Fit F20. Key to RUN.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV44 Wideband AFR gauge ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: 10-way connector A on the back of the gauge (replacement pins JST SPUD-001T-P0.5), taking AEM's own Power / IO cable 35-3430 with loose leads: red switched 12 V, black ground, white / black CANH, green / black CANL. The 8-way connector B takes AEM's sensor cable 35-3427, never cut - confirm
expect: The gauge powers at RUN; the client shows frame 0x180 arriving on CAN2

do: MG23 - start, then the first idle
how:
Factory side: the starter's small S terminal has the factory BW wire from the inhibitor switch; the switch's BY comes from the key. Unplug, label, tape back. New side: K9's terminal 87 lead (10 AWG red, capped at E27) onto the starter's S terminal. The inhibitor's start pair was joined at MG12: BY through 8.2 kOhm to L1-S1 11, BW to block ground. Read A4 now if E27 could not: CRANK_OK in P and N only. Enable O21 START_RLY (7.0 A). Set the client logging for CK14: A4 raw, A16 raw, supply voltage and both decoded states at the fastest rate; meter on min/max between the engine block and the dash ground bus. Lever in P, headlamps off: crank until it starts. At the first idle read A7 and enter OIL_MIN from it. Stop; crank again with the headlamps switched on just before START. Try START in R and D: nothing. Label everything, save a new revision.
The plug that moves here, and how its end is made:
DV02 Starter ends in a heat-shrink ring or spade on the part's own stud, screw or tab. Its plug: Main B stud for a ring lug, plus the S terminal on factory connector A-01, 1 wire on the diagram (BW on an automatic); the stud thread, and whether A-01 is a bare push-on terminal or a 1-way housing: not known - confirm
DV03 Start relay K9 ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: Sealed mini ISO relay, SPDT (Picker PC792E-1C-C-12S-DN-X), in a Chief 75340 weatherproof 5-way harness-mount relay connector; by Waytek's listing the connector comes without its terminals and seals - confirm
expect: Cranks only in P and N; starts and idles; the pump holds on after the prime because oil_ok latches; A16 reads START for the whole crank and A4 holds CRANK_OK; block offset under 0.74 V
caution: Garage door open. Belt and fan clear. An engine that starts and dies about 3 s later with zero oil pressure shown is the oil gate, not the PMU: check the oil, then the sender wire.

do: Key out: hazards, horn, winks, brake
how: Car asleep, key out, doors shut. Hazard switch on: all four corners flash; leave them a minute, switch off. Horn pad: both horns. Left wink button alone, then the right alone. Brake pedal.
expect: Each works from asleep. Hazards at 1.5 Hz. Each wink raises its own lamp only and lowers it on release. Brake lamps light

do: Key out: the lamps on their own fuses
how: Interior lamp switch to DOOR: open the driver door, shut it, open the passenger door. Switch to ON, then OFF. Open the glove box. Open the luggage lid or cover that works the luggage lamp.
expect: Interior lamp follows either door on DOOR and is steady on ON; glove box and luggage lamps follow their lids

do: Key out: confirm it goes back to sleep
how: Everything off, doors shut, hands off. Watch the client, or listen at the node for relay K11 dropping out.
expect: K11 drops and the PMU sleeps 30 s after the last change

how: Key to ACC. Head unit on, USB-C charging, the display boots. Press the rear-defog key on the climate panel, then press it again to switch off.
expect: Head unit, USB-C and display on; the defog output follows the panel key; the fuel pump and the coils stay off

do: RUN, engine off: fuel pump and ignition
how: Key to RUN. Listen for the pump.
expect: The pump runs for 3 s and stops; the coils have 12 V; the display shows zero oil pressure

how: Stalk to LOW, HIGH, back to OFF from HIGH, then OFF from LOW. INT for three sweeps. A quick flick of LOW. Hold WASH for two seconds and let go.
expect: Two speeds; parks at the bottom from both; INT pauses 3 s; one flick is one sweep; the pump runs only while held and the wipers make two more sweeps
caution: Wet the glass first.

how: Light switch PARK: tail, front park, four side markers, licence, and the dash illumination. HEAD: low beams, and the pop-ups rise. Dimmer high: high beams and the tell-tale. Pull PASS with the lights off: the high beams flash - note whether the pop-ups move, the record does not say. Change the dimmer setting, which is the control panel's: the dash lamps and the display dim. Back to OFF: the pop-ups drop.
expect: Every lamp named lights; pop-ups up on HEAD and down on OFF; dimming works
caution: Stand clear of the pop-ups.

do: RUN: turn signals, hazard override, reverse
how: Stalk left, then right: check front, rear and the arrow on the display, and count the rate. With the stalk left, switch the hazards on. Foot on the brake, lever to R: reverse lamps. Lever back to P.
expect: 1.5 Hz each side; hazards take over from the stalk; reverse lamps only in R
caution: Wheels chocked; engine off for the lever test.

how: Foot on the brake. Lever in R: key to START. Lever in D: key to START. Then N: START. Then P: START and let it run.
expect: No crank in R or D; cranks in N and in P; the engine starts

how: At idle: the pump stays on, the charge warning goes out, oil pressure shows. Repeat wipers, lights with pop-ups, turn signals, brake, horn and the defog key with the engine running. Watch the client for any output in status 2, 3 or 7.
expect: Everything works as before; every active output reads status 1; supply voltage is in the charging range seen at E12
caution: Garage door open.

how: Start the stopwatch. Stop the engine, open the master disconnect. Unlatch and unplug the PMU's 39-way connector. From the kit, run the three jumpers from the dash-node busbar: the 10 A one onto relay K13's terminal 30, where the O5 wire arrives - never terminal 87; the 20 A one onto the O12 splice; the 5 A pushbutton one onto the K9 terminal 86 lead at the node. Lever in P. Close the disconnect, key to RUN, press the pushbutton to crank. Let it idle a minute. Turn the key off: the engine must stop. Stop the stopwatch.
expect: The engine starts and runs on the jumpers and stops with the key. Under about twenty minutes from start to running
caution: With the module out there is no inhibitor: the lever is in P before the pushbutton is touched. Ignition is live whenever the disconnect is closed. No oil gate: if it stalls, key off at once.

how: Open the disconnect. Remove all three jumpers and put them back in the kit bag. Plug the 39-way in and latch its lever. Close the disconnect. Start the engine normally and repeat the lamps and wipers once.
expect: Nothing temporary left at the node; the car works as before
caution: A limp-home wire left in place is the next fault.

do: Save the configuration as a new revision
how: Save to the PMU and to the laptop as the next revision. Put a copy of the file with the USB-to-CAN cable for the glovebox, and one where it can come back to the project.
expect: The same revision in the PMU, on the laptop and on the car's copy

do: Take the whole-car sleeping current, one hour after key-off
how: Key out, doors shut, laptop unplugged from DP-DIAG. Wait one hour so every timer has run out. Clamp meter around the battery negative cable in the cargo bin, or a meter on its mA range in series at the disconnect.
expect: 50 mA or under; 30 mA is the target
caution: A meter in series on its mA range will blow its fuse if anything wakes the car. Do not open a door with it in circuit.

do: Walk the car and check every factory end is labelled
how: Go device by device in the migration order. Every factory plug that was taken off a device carries a MIGRATED label and a date and is taped back.
expect: No unlabelled factory plug anywhere

do: Look for anything still connected to the factory harness
how: Follow each factory harness by hand from end to end. Anything still plugged into a device is a circuit no migration row moved.
expect: Nothing is still plugged in
caution: If something is, stop and note it before unplugging. Do not guess what it fed.

do: Open the disconnect; take the factory feed and ground off the new backbone
how: Master disconnect OFF. At the dash node take the factory main feed's lug, with its fusible links, off the busbar stud. Re-torque the busbar nut for what is left on it and paint-mark it. At the front star stud take the factory main ground off.
expect: Nothing factory is left on the busbar or the front star

how: Photograph each first. Engine harness from front harness at X-01 (22-cavity). Dash harness at X-02 and X-12. Rear harness at X-03, left side behind the door. Transmission harness at X-10 and the two single plugs X-17. Parking-brake harness at X-11. Label both halves of each.
expect: Each harness is free of the others

do: Take out the dash harness with the factory cluster
how: The cluster is on two 13-cavity round plugs: leave them plugged in and lift harness and cluster out together. Release each clip; never pull on the wires.
expect: Dash harness and cluster out as one piece

do: Take out the front harness with the fuse box, relays and control unit
how: Unbolt the fuse block under the dash and the control unit; free the relays from their mounts - the horn relay is toward the engine bay or cowl. Feed the harness back through its grommets. Take the body-ground lugs off at the left suspension tower and under the dash on the left, and wherever else a black wire ends on the body.
expect: Front harness out with the fuse block, relays and control unit still attached
caution: Do not cut a wire to get a connector through a grommet. Ease the grommet out of the panel instead.

how: Free it from the engine and the firewall. Every sender, coil and alternator plug has already been moved. Anything left on it is emission or choke equipment the new harness does not serve: note what it was on before unplugging.
expect: Engine harness out in one piece

do: Take out the rear and transmission harnesses
how: Rear harness: from X-03 rearward, off its ground points. Transmission harness: its plugs at X-10 and X-17 are already parted; free it from the transmission and lift it out.
expect: Both out in one piece

how: Walk the new harness: every Deutsch plug latched, every device end still joined, the wideband gauge still on F20 and CAN2, the A/C compressor's clutch plug still unplugged and nothing else of the A/C disturbed.
expect: Nothing of the new harness moved

how: Coil each harness loosely, connectors labelled, fuse block and cluster padded. One box. Write the date on it and keep it until the shakedown is passed (E34).
expect: One box, nothing cut, nothing kinked

do: Close the disconnect and prove the car
how: Disconnect ON. Start the engine. Run through lights, pop-ups, wipers, turn signals, brake lamps and horn once.
expect: Everything works exactly as at E29
caution: Garage door open.

how: It was unplugged at the strip (S1) and plugged back at E12 so the meters read. It is wherever E12 left it, with the dash out.
expect: Cluster in hand, face up

how: Read the main odometer, not the trip counter. Read every digit left to right, including the tenths wheel if it has one.
expect: One figure, in miles

how: A clear photo of the odometer window with the torch on it.
expect: The digits are readable in the photo

how: Type the whole miles on this row. Put the tenths, if any, in a note.
expect: The row shows the value in mi

how: Key out, doors shut, hazards off, hands off everything. Wait a full minute.
expect: The PMU is asleep: relay K11 at the node has dropped out

how: The helper films the horn pad and listens at the nose, or works the stopwatch. Press the pad once, firmly, and hold it for a second. Time from the press to the first sound.
expect: A delay in milliseconds

do: Repeat twice more, sleeping the car each time
how: Wait a minute between presses so each one starts from asleep. Take the longest of the three.
expect: Three readings; the longest is the answer

do: Time the brake lamps the same way
how: Car asleep again. The helper watches or films the brake lamps. Press the pedal. Time from the press to the lamps lighting.
expect: A second delay in milliseconds

how: The horn's longest reading on this row, in ms. The brake figure in a note.
expect: Row saved

do: Pick a cold morning and leave the car asleep
how: The first cold start of the shakedown (E31) is a good day: take this before the key goes in. Read the air temperature.
expect: Car untouched overnight; temperature noted

how: Opening the door wakes the PMU, so get in, shut the door, keep your hands off everything and wait a full minute. Then press the pad once and hold it a second. Time from the press to the first sound, as in Q-110.
expect: A delay in milliseconds

how: The figure on this row in ms; the temperature in a note.
expect: Row saved

do: Open the disconnect and fit relays K3 and K4
how: Dash node, the two sockets labelled HATCH-REL (K3) and FUEL-REL (K4). Push a micro relay into each until it seats.
expect: Both relays seated

do: Check F33's holder, and leave the fuse out for now
how: F33 is the sealed inline holder on the release branch off O10, ahead of the two relays. Leave it empty until the solenoids are joined.
expect: Holder found and labelled RELEASE; no fuse in it

how:
At the hatch latch. The new wire L4-M 3 (14 AWG orange) comes up the hinge loop. Join it to the solenoid's + side, the factory GR lead: a sealed butt splice onto the lead, or a ring or spade if the solenoid has a terminal. Leave the solenoid's B lead on its factory ground.
The plug this end takes, and how it is made:
DV48 Hatch-release solenoid keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector H-14, 2 wires on the diagram (GR, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: L4-M 3 on the solenoid's +; the label reads L4-M-3

how: Meter on continuity from the solenoid's B side to bare body metal.
expect: The meter beeps
caution: No beep means the factory ground is gone. Do not rely on the latch's bolts: note it.

do: Join the fuel-door solenoid and prove its ground
how:
Behind the driver-side rear quarter trim. L4-M 4 (14 AWG orange) to the solenoid's + side, the factory GB lead, the same way. Continuity from its B side to the body.
The plug this end takes, and how it is made:
DV49 Fuel-door release solenoid keeps its factory plug: the harness half is cut off the old harness with 150 mm of lead when this circuit moves (E28) and spliced onto the new wires, colour to colour (D-537). Its plug: Factory connector H-16, 2 wires on the diagram (GB, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: L4-M 4 on the solenoid's +; ground beeps

how: Before the car's own circuit is used: ammeter in series with the fused test lead, 12 V straight onto each solenoid's + for half a second, one at a time. Write both figures down.
expect: Each solenoid pulls its latch; two readings in amps
caution: Half a second only. A release solenoid is not made to be held on.

how: The replacement switch P165 goes in place of the broken one. Where its wires land is not in the record yet: if the release design (A11) has written it by now, follow it; if not, fit the switch mechanically, leave its leads insulated and note it.
expect: Switch fitted

do: Fit F33 and close the disconnect
how: 10 A blade fuse into F33's holder. Disconnect ON. Key to ACC and watch both latches.
expect: Nothing moves when the key is turned on
caution: The relays are live whenever O10 is on. If a latch fires by itself, key off and pull F33.

do: Release the hatch from its key
how: Key at ACC, car standing. Press the hatch key on the left plate. In the client watch O10's current.
expect: K3 clicks, the hatch pops, the pulse is over in well under 1.5 s; O10 does not trip

do: Release the fuel door from its key
how: Press the fuel-door key.
expect: K4 clicks, the fuel door pops; O10 does not trip

do: Try both with the key out
how: Key out, car awake or asleep. Press each key once.
expect: Each releases: the PMU wakes, O10 comes up for the length of the pulse, and drops again

do: Ten releases each, then check F33
how: Ten presses of each key, a few seconds apart. Then pull F33 and look at it.
expect: Every press releases; F33 is not discoloured or blown

do: Open the disconnect and take the driver door trim off
how: Glass up and taped. Winder handle, inner handle cover, arm rest, trim panel, then peel the water shield back carefully - it goes back on. Bag and label every fastener. This order is from the 1985 manual: confirm on the car.
expect: Bare door, shield intact

do: Unplug D1 at the sill and empty the door plug
how: Behind the driver kick panel, unlatch D1. In the door-side plug pull the wedgelock, then take the sealing plugs out of cavities 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8. Leave cavity 3's plug in.
expect: Seven open cavities; cavity 3 sealed
