do: Pass the door harness through the jamb boot
how: Tape the eight-wire bundle to the pull wire, lead it through the boot from the body side into the door. Leave enough at the sill end to reach D1 with the door fully open and fully shut.
expect: Harness through; the door swings without pulling it
caution: Do not slit the boot. It is what keeps water out of the sill.

do: Crimp and insert the seven contacts
how: Socket contacts, size 16; the two 14 AWG window wires take the 14 AWG contact. Strip, crimp, tug. Insert by the number moulded on the plug: 1 window leg A (14 AWG red) - 2 window leg B (14 AWG red) - 4 mirror common (grey) - 5 mirror motor (grey) - 6 mirror clutch (grey) - 7 mirror heat (16 AWG red) - 8 door ground (black). Each clicks; tug each. Wedgelock back in.
expect: Seven clicks; nothing pulls out
caution: Eye protection when crimping and cutting.

do: Run the wires inside the door
how: Window legs 1 and 2 to where the regulator's motor will sit - the door drawing gives the place. Mirror wires 4, 5, 6 and 7 to the mirror's plug inside the door. Ground 8 with the mirror group. Clip the bundle to the door frame clear of the glass's path and the regulator arms.
expect: Nothing in the path of the glass; run the glass down and up by hand to check

do: End the window legs in their plug
how: Cavities 1 and 2 end at the motor's place in the Deutsch plug the door drawing gives. Dust cap on it. Label it D1-1/2 WINDOW.
expect: A capped 2-way plug where the motor will sit

do: Join or cap the mirror wires
how: If the mirror's leads have been measured and the door drawing says which is which: join 4, 5 and 6 to the mirror head's factory leads with sealed butt splices, 7 to the heater lead, 8 to the ground lead. If not: cap each wire with adhesive heat-shrink and label it by cavity.
expect: Each mirror wire joined or capped, every one labelled

how: Meter on continuity. With D1 still unplugged at the sill: each door-plug cavity to its far end beeps; each to its neighbours and to the door shell does not. Then mate D1 and check cavity 8's far end to the sill ground stud.
expect: Seven good wires; no shorts; ground beeps to the sill stud

how: Seat the boot at both ends. Water shield back on and sealed all round. Trim panel, arm rest, handle cover, winder handle. Latch D1 at the sill node.
expect: Door trimmed; D1 latched

do: Do the passenger door the same way
how: Plug D2. Same cavities. The only difference is at the sill: cavity 5 is the right mirror's motor line and cavity 6 its clutch line.
expect: Passenger door wired, tested, trimmed; D2 latched

do: Leave the window fuses out and close the disconnect
how: F8 and F9 holders at the sill stay empty until the regulators are fitted. Check F14 (5 A) is in. Disconnect ON.
expect: F8 and F9 empty; nothing in either door is live

do: Open the disconnect and mount the comfort block
how: Behind the centre stack, within reach of the L3-CMF receptacle, cover facing where a hand can get to it, clear of the heater case and of anything that drips.
expect: Block fixed; its cover opens with the stack in

how:
The block's 12 AWG red input lead has a ring on the block's stud and a DTP 2-way plug on the other end: contact in cavity 1, sealing plug in cavity 2. Take the dust cap off L3-CMF and plug in. Tighten the stud nut.
The plug this end takes, and how it is made:
DV56 O15 comfort block C ends in one of our own Deutsch pairs. Its plug: Blue Sea 5028: a #10-32 input stud for a ring terminal and a screw terminal per circuit; its 12 AWG feed lead is ours and ends in a DTP06-2S plug (terminals not seen, confirm) into our Deutsch DTP04-2P receptacle L3-CMF
expect: Latched; input lead tight on the stud

do: Fit the five fuses and label the block
how: Position 1: 7.5 A (F25, SEAT-D-HEAT). 2: 7.5 A (F26, SEAT-P-HEAT). 3: 5 A (F27, SEAT-D-COOL). 4: 5 A (F28, SEAT-P-COOL). 5: 7.5 A (F29, DCU-CMF). 6: empty. Label each position on the block.
expect: Five fuses in the right places

how: From the block and the climate unit down the driver side of the tunnel and under where the carpet will lie, to under the driver's seat. It carries four 16 AWG wires for the 4-way L3-SD and two 12 AWG for the 2-way L3-SDM. Tape every 150 mm; keep it off seat-rail bolts and sharp floor edges.
expect: Six wires reach under the driver's seat with slack for the seat to slide

how:
L3-SD, DT 4-way: 1 heater + (red, from F25) - 2 cooling fan + (red, from F27) - 3 heater - - 4 cooling fan -. L3-SDM, DTP 2-way, size-12 contacts: 1 motor feed (12 AWG red, from K14 terminal 87) - 2 motor return (12 AWG black). Click, tug, wedgelocks in. Dust caps on. Tie both where a hand can reach them through the carpet's seat opening.
The plug this end takes, and how it is made:
DV57 Driver seat ends in one of our own Deutsch pairs. Its plug: RECARO Ergomed ES with the Climate Package (luxury LP52): the seat's own connectors are not known - no installation sheet was found (confirm; adapter lead A19 owns them). The leg ends under the seat in our Deutsch receptacles, a DT04-4P for heat and cool and a DTP04-2P for the motor feed: L3-SD and L3-SDM
expect: Two capped receptacles under the driver's seat, labelled L3-SD and L3-SDM

do: Do the passenger side the same
how:
Down the passenger side of the tunnel. L3-SP: 1 heater + (from F26) - 2 fan + (from F28) - 3 heater - - 4 fan -. L3-SPM: 1 motor feed (from K15 terminal 87) - 2 motor return.
The plug this end takes, and how it is made:
DV58 Passenger seat ends in one of our own Deutsch pairs. Its plug: RECARO Ergomed ES with the Climate Package (luxury LP52): the seat's own connectors are not known - no installation sheet was found (confirm; adapter lead A19 owns them). The leg ends under the seat in our Deutsch receptacles, a DT04-4P for heat and cool and a DTP04-2P for the motor feed: L3-SP and L3-SPM
expect: Two capped receptacles under the passenger seat

do: Fit the seat relays and their fuses at the node
how: Dash node: relays into the sockets labelled SEAT-D (K14) and SEAT-P (K15). A 25 A MAXI fuse into each of the two holders at the busbar stud, F35 and F36.
expect: K14, K15 seated; F35, F36 in

how: The 8-way plug for the climate unit's comfort connector: 1 driver heat return (from L3-SD 3) - 2 passenger heat return (from L3-SP 3) - 3 driver cool return (from L3-SD 4) - 4 passenger cool return (from L3-SP 4) - 5 supply (16 AWG red, from F29) - 6, 7 and 8 ground (14 AWG black each; these take the 14 AWG contact). Wedgelock in. Plug it into the climate unit's 8-way receptacle.
expect: Eight contacts in, plug latched

do: Land the grounds on the dash ground bus
how: Three 14 AWG black from DP-DCU-C 6, 7 and 8, and two 12 AWG black from L3-SDM 2 and L3-SPM 2: each on its own ring on the dash ground bus.
expect: Five rings on the ground bus, tight

how: Meter on continuity, DP-DCU-C unplugged again for this. L3-SD 1 to block position 1; L3-SD 2 to position 3; L3-SD 3 to DP-DCU-C 1; L3-SD 4 to DP-DCU-C 3. L3-SP 1 to position 2; L3-SP 2 to position 4; L3-SP 3 to DP-DCU-C 2; L3-SP 4 to DP-DCU-C 4. L3-SDM 1 to K14's 87; L3-SPM 1 to K15's 87; both cavity 2s to the ground bus. Nothing to its neighbour, nothing to the body except the grounds.
expect: Every wire reaches its own end and no other

do: Power it and check the feeds
how: DP-DCU-C back in. Disconnect ON. Enable O15 COMFORT in the client; the record gives it no limit - set one and note it. Key to RUN. Meter on DC volts to ground at: the block's stud; L3-SD 1 and 2; L3-SP 1 and 2; L3-SDM 1; L3-SPM 1.
expect: K14 and K15 click at RUN; battery voltage at all seven points; 0 V at all of them with the key at ACC

do: Check the climate unit switches each return
how: Test lamp between L3-SD 1 and L3-SD 3. Turn the driver's seat heat on at the panel's seat knob: the lamp lights; off: it goes out. Repeat for driver cooling (2 and 4) and both passenger pairs at L3-SP.
expect: Four lamps, each following its own control and no other

do: Cap, label and close the disconnect
how: Dust caps back on all four receptacles. Label each. Disconnect as you need it for the next row.
expect: Four capped, labelled receptacles under the seats

do: Open the disconnect and lay the lead set
how: Nine 16 AWG wires from behind the climate unit, across the dash rail and down the centre to the heater case. Keep the bundle away from the blower's 12 AWG feed where you can.
expect: Nine wires reach the heater case with slack

how: Socket contacts, size 16. By the moulded numbers: 1 mode signal (blue) - 2 blend signal (blue) - 3 recirculate signal (blue) - 4 servo +5 V (pink) - 5 servo ground (black) - 6 blower speed (blue) - 7 blower speed ground (black) - 8 cabin sensor (grey) - 9 sensor return (black). Sealing plugs in 10, 11 and 12. Wedgelock in. Label every wire at both ends as it is cut.
expect: Nine clicks, three sealing plugs
caution: Three blue signal wires look alike. Label each before the next is cut.

do: Split the 5 V and the ground into three at the heater case
how: Cut each of the three servo extension leads so the servo-side plug keeps its tail. Join all three +5 V tails to the pink wire with one sealed butt splice, and all three ground tails to the black wire with another. Use the splice size that takes the combined strands.
expect: One pink into three; one black into three

do: Join each signal wire to its servo lead
how:
Mode: cavity 1's blue to the first lead's signal wire. Blend: cavity 2's. Recirculate: cavity 3's. A sealed butt splice each. Shrink them.
The plug this end takes, and how it is made:
DV59 HVAC door servos x3 ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: Each FEETECH FS5115M has a 30 cm (12 in) lead ending in a JR-style connector, Futaba-compatible; Pololu's page gives neither its pin count nor its gender (3 conductors by the devices row). The harness end is a JR extension lead, cut and spliced to the DP-DCU-D conductors at the HVAC case - confirm
expect: Three servo plugs, each with signal, 5 V and ground

do: Label and park the three servo leads
how: Label each plug MODE, BLEND, RECIRC. Tie each near its door's cable on the heater case, plug end covered.
expect: Three labelled leads, out of the way of the pedals and the heater doors

do: End the blower-speed pair at the resistor pack's hole
how:
Cavities 6 and 7's pair runs to the old resistor pack's hole in the heater case, beside the capped L3-BLW receptacle. Fold each end back, adhesive heat-shrink over it, label DP-DCU-D-6 / CAPPED and DP-DCU-D-7 / CAPPED.
The plug this end takes, and how it is made:
DV55 Blower final stage ends in one of our own Deutsch pairs. Its plug: Pololu G2 24v21 (#2995): a bare board, no plug of its own - VIN, GND, OUTA and OUTB on 5 mm-pitch holes for the two 2-way screw terminal blocks in the box (rated 16 A), logic on 0.1 in header holes. Its adapter lead is ours and is not drawn yet (confirm); it plugs into L3-BLW
DV27 Blower motor ends in one of our own Deutsch pairs. Its plug: New motor, Four Seasons 35483 class, 2 wires; the maker's own connector is not known (one search found no sheet). The leg ends in our Deutsch DTP04-2P receptacle and the motor's lead takes the DTP06-2S plug - confirm the motor's lead; housing L3-BLW
expect: Two capped, labelled ends beside L3-BLW

how: The thermistor on cavities 8 and 9's pair, at a shaded spot on the dash away from the heater outlets and the sun. The record does not say where: choose, and note it.
expect: Sensor fixed, its pair clipped

how: Meter on continuity, plug not yet in the unit. Cavity 1 to the MODE plug's signal pin; 2 to BLEND; 3 to RECIRC. Cavity 4 to the +5 V pin of all three plugs; cavity 5 to the ground pin of all three. 6 and 7 to their capped ends. Across 8 and 9 read ohms: a 10 kOhm thermistor reads about 10 kOhm at room temperature.
expect: All through; no wire reaches a neighbour; the sensor reads in the thousands of ohms, not open and not zero

how: DP-DCU-D into the upper-row receptacle. Disconnect ON. In the client watch frame 0x300, byte 3: the cabin temperature. If the comfort block is in (E38) and the key is at RUN, meter the MODE plug: 5 V between its +5 V and ground pins.
expect: Cabin temperature near the garage's; 5 V at the servo plugs once the comfort supply is there - whether the rail is up at rest is not in the record: confirm
caution: Do not plug a servo in to try it: the endpoints are not calibrated and it will drive a door cable against its stop.

do: Open the disconnect and make the hatch run
how: Three 16 AWG grey wires. One end: a 4-way plug to mate L4-RDR at the rear node, socket contacts in cavities 1, 2, 3, sealing plug in 4. The other end: the L4-HRD receptacle, pin contacts in 1, 2, 3, sealing plug in 4. Wire 1 to 1, 2 to 2, 3 to 3. Label both ends.
expect: A three-wire lead with a plug at one end and a receptacle at the other

do: Route it up the hinge loop
how: From the rear node alongside the tail-lamp wires, through the hatch hinge loop, to behind the hatch trim. Open the hatch fully and set the slack there; then close it and check nothing is pinched.
expect: The hatch moves through its whole travel without tightening the loop
caution: Keep fingers out of the hinge. Prop the hatch if its struts are weak.

how: Clip the receptacle behind the hatch trim where a hand can reach it with the trim off. Dust cap on. Label it L4-HRD. Plug the other end into L4-RDR at the rear node.
expect: Capped receptacle in the hatch; plug latched at the rear node

do: Test the rear run end to end
how: Meter on continuity from L3-RDR behind the dash to L4-HRD in the hatch: cavity 1 to 1, 2 to 2, 3 to 3. A helper or the long lead makes this a one-person job. Then each to its neighbours and to the body.
expect: Three beeps; no crosses; nothing to the body

do: Route the front run to the nose
how: The three grey wires from L2-R at the dash post follow the front leg through the cowl grommet and along the inner wing to the nose, then along the bumper beam. Tape to the leg every 150 mm.
expect: Three wires at the front bumper with a coil of slack

how: Receptacle L2-RDR: pin contacts in 1, 2, 3, sealing plug in 4. Mount it behind the front bumper, facing down or sideways so it cannot fill with water. Dust cap on. Label it.
expect: Capped receptacle behind the bumper

do: Plug L2-R in at the dash post and check the node tails
how: L2-R's plug onto its receptacle at the post. On the node side its three wires end as short tails: each folded back, heat-shrunk and labelled. Beside them the receiver's feed: one red tail off O10 and a ground ring on the ground bus, the red capped and labelled.
expect: Four capped tails at the node: three sensor wires and one feed

how: Continuity from each node tail to its cavity at L2-RDR: 1, 2, 3. Then each to its neighbours and to the body. Re-cap the tails.
expect: Three beeps; no crosses

do: Close the disconnect and check the feed tail
how: Disconnect ON, key to ACC. Meter from the capped red feed tail to ground - probe through the cap's end, then re-seal it.
expect: Battery voltage at ACC, 0 V with the car asleep
caution: That tail is live whenever O10 is on. It must stay capped.

do: Open the disconnect and check it is dead at the output stud
how: Master disconnect OFF. Meter from the disconnect's output stud to the rear star stud.
expect: 0 V
caution: The output stud is on the battery through one switch. Rings and watch off.

how: The terminal-mount fuse holder for the amplifier goes on the disconnect's output stud beside the starter's. How the two stack is not settled in the record: fit it the way that keeps every lug flat and note it. No fuse in it. Re-torque the stud's nut to the maker's figure (confirm) and paint-mark it.
expect: Holder on, no fuse, the starter's holder and the 2 AWG lug undisturbed and tight
caution: This stud carries the starter cable and the main feed. If you loosen it, it must be torqued again.

do: Make and run the 4 AWG feed
how: 4 AWG red from the F34 holder to the amplifier's place in the passenger bin, kept inside the bin. Hydraulic-crimp a lug on the holder end; heavy-wall heat-shrink and a red boot. Leave the amplifier end long, capped with heat-shrink and labelled C13 / AMP +.
expect: Feed in place; dead, because F34 is empty

do: Make and run the 4 AWG return
how: 4 AWG black from the amplifier's place to the rear star stud. Lug on the stud end, torqued with the others on that stud; cavity wax. Amplifier end capped and labelled C14 / AMP -.
expect: Return on the rear star; continuity from its capped end to the battery negative post

do: Run the signal cable, remote and microphone leads
how:
From behind the head unit, along the passenger sill under the carpet line, to the passenger bin: the six-channel shielded cable, the 18 AWG blue remote wire from the head unit's blue/white, and the microphone lead coming down from the A-pillar. Tape them together; keep them off the rear leg's bundle.
The plug this end takes, and how it is made:
DV28 Head unit ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: Pioneer DMH-W4660NEX (luxury LP55): the maker's installation sheet was not reached, so the unit's power connector, its ways and whether its power cord is in the box are not known. The devices row assumes a cord with red, yellow, orange, black and blue / white leads, RCA pre-outs and a microphone lead - confirm
DV60 Amplifier / DSP ends in a new mating connector, bought for it (D-543). Its plug: Not picked (luxury LP57, status hold), so its terminals cannot be known until it is; adapter lead A22 owns the speaker, remote and pre-amp end, which has no connector drawn yet - confirm
expect: Three cables from the dash to the bin, labelled at both ends

how: From the bin forward under the carpet line: one twisted pair to the driver kick panel and one to the A-pillar base on the driver sill; one each to the passenger kick panel and A-pillar base on the passenger sill; one up the tunnel side to the console between the seats.
expect: Five pairs at their places with slack

do: Run the rear and sub pairs
how: One pair to each rear quarter trim position. Two pairs across the cargo floor behind the seats to the driver-side cargo bin.
expect: Four more pairs at their places

do: Pin and cap the seven 2-way receptacles
how: At each end: pin contacts, + wire in cavity 1, - wire in cavity 2, wedgelock, dust cap. Label each with its code: L3-SPF-L, L3-SPF-R, L3-TW-L, L3-TW-R, L3-CTR, L4-SPR-L, L4-SPR-R.
expect: Seven capped, labelled receptacles
caution: Mark + on each pair at the bin end as you pin the far end. Once the trim is on you cannot follow a wire.

how:
L4-SUB in the driver-side cargo bin: first pair + to cavity 1 and - to 2; second pair + to 3 and - to 4. Wedgelock, dust cap, label.
The plug this end takes, and how it is made:
DV61 Subwoofer enclosure ends in one of our own Deutsch pairs. Its plug: Not picked (luxury LP61 the driver, LP62 the enclosure, made): the driver's terminals cannot be known until it is (confirm; adapter lead A21 owns them). The leg ends in our Deutsch DT04-4P receptacle in the driver-side bin, the driver's lead taking the DT06-4S plug: L4-SUB
expect: One capped 4-way

how: Meter on continuity at the bin end. For each pair: short cavities 1 and 2 together at the far end with a jumper - the pair beeps; remove the jumper - it does not. Then each conductor to the body and to the next pair.
expect: Nine pairs through; none to the body; none to another

do: Coil, label and tidy the bin end
how: Label every cable at the bin with its far end's code. Coil the spare length where the amplifier will sit. Nothing bare.
expect: Bin end reads like a list

do: Close the disconnect and check nothing changed
how: Disconnect ON. The car powers as before; the capped 4 AWG feed reads 0 V to ground because F34 is empty.
expect: Car normal; amplifier feed dead

do: Walk every cabin connector before anything covers it
how: Disconnect OPEN. At the dash post: every leg plug latched, wedgelocks in, sealing plugs in every empty cavity. At the instrument unit and the climate unit: every tail latched. At the sill node: D1 and D2 latched, relays seated, F14 in, F8 and F9 empty and labelled. Tug each plug once.
expect: Nothing pulls off; nothing unlabelled

do: Check the water rule at the node
how: Every bundle arrives at the dash node, the PMU and each receptacle from below or through a drip loop. The PMU's connector faces down or sideways. Nothing sits in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell. Busbar cover on.
expect: A drip run down any bundle would fall off before it reached a connector

do: Final-wrap and tie down every cabin loom
how: Cloth tape over each bundle, half-overlapped, from the dash post outward: the dash leg to the column and centre stack, the tails to both units, the sill run, the rear leg into the tunnel, the seat harnesses, the audio cables. Clear heat-shrink over any label a wrap would hide. Clip or tie every run so nothing hangs or rubs.
expect: No loose wire anywhere in the cabin; every label still readable
caution: Do not wrap the engine-bay looms today. They wait for E33.

how: Every node, every plug group and every run where it lies: dash node from each side, both units' rear walls, the column, the sill node, the tunnel, under each seat, both sills, the rear node. These photos are the as-built record.
expect: A photo of everything trim is about to hide

do: Check what the carpet will cover
how: Tunnel: the heavy cables, the rear leg and the pull string lie flat and clipped. Sills: the audio cables on one side apart from the power bundle. Under each seat: the 4-way and the 2-way receptacles capped, labelled and tied where a hand reaches through the carpet's opening. No cable across a seat-rail bolt hole.
expect: Nothing under the carpet line can be pinched by a seat rail or a sill plate

how: Lay it from the tunnel outward. Bring each seat receptacle up through or beside the carpet as it was placed.
expect: Carpet flat; four receptacles reachable

how: Driver side first: look once more at the sill node, then fit the kick panel over it. The speaker receptacle behind each kick panel stays capped and reachable. Sill plates on with their own screws from the bags.
expect: Both kick panels and both sill plates on; no screw through a cable
caution: Know where the cables run under each plate before driving a screw.

do: Close the disconnect and run a quick function check
how: Lights, turn signals, wipers, horn, brake lamps, door lamp. The dash is still open, so a fault is still easy.
expect: Everything works as at E29

how: Climate unit seated in its opening with every rear plug latched and no loom trapped behind it. Head unit in, its wires as joined at MG02. The comfort fuse block's cover can still be opened. Centre panel, heater wire, knobs and ash tray per the bags.
expect: Centre stack in; the climate panel and head unit work

how: Offer the instrument panel up over the node. Before it seats, check the tails to the instrument unit and the glovebox are not trapped and the two capped receptacles behind the dash are tied back. The manual shows 4 fixing bolts for the panel - confirm on the car. Then grilles, garnishes, ventilator louvers and switch panels from their bags. The left plate goes to the left of the steering wheel on its own cable.
expect: Dash fixed; nothing rattles; no loom visible
caution: Do not use a bolt to pull the dash into place. If it will not seat, something is behind it.

how: Glove compartment and lid in. The laptop port DP-DIAG sits inside where a plug can reach it. The glove box lamp and its lid switch work.
expect: The port is reachable with the lid open; the lamp follows the lid

how: The instrument unit on its plate in the instrument opening, both rear plugs latched. Meter hood over it; the manual's view lists a pair of bolts beside the hood - confirm on the car. Column covers, upper and lower. If the steering wheel came off: nut to 40 to 50 N-m, horn cap on.
expect: Display in place and lit at RUN; column covers on

how: Rear console, coin box, brake cover and shift lever knob from their bags. The centre speaker's capped receptacle stays reachable under the console. The parking-brake warning still shows with the lever up.
expect: Console in; the lever moves through every gear; brake warning works

how: Each seat on its own mounting bolts from the bags. Tighten firmly and check for looseness; the record has no torque for them. If a seat-belt anchor came off: 39 to 55 N-m. Slide each seat fully both ways: the under-seat receptacles and their harness do not move with it.
expect: Seats solid; belts latch; nothing under a seat is touched by the rails
caution: Seat and belt bolts are safety fasteners. If one is missing or its thread is poor, do not drive.

how: Before it goes on: the battery hold-down tight, boots on both terminals, Class-T cover on, the rear node's plugs latched, the capped radar, amplifier and sub ends tied back. Then the cargo-bin trim. The master disconnect must still be reachable from the hatch.
expect: Trim on; the disconnect can be turned from the open hatch

do: Full function pass with the car whole
how: Repeat E29's pass: key out, ACC, RUN, engine running. Every lamp, pop-ups, wipers and washer, horn, turn signals and hazards, brake and reverse lamps, releases, defog key, display. Then put the car to sleep and wake it with a door.
expect: Everything works; no warning on the display; the client shows no output in status 2, 3 or 7
caution: Garage door open with the engine running.

how: Every bag from the strip is empty.
expect: No fastener left over

do: Before the first drive: the stuck-on check
how: In the garage, engine off, key at RUN, client connected. For each of O2 (low beam), O3 (high beam), O5 (fuel pump), O7 (brake) and O12 (ignition) in turn: make sure it is commanded off and read its measured voltage.
expect: Zero on all five
caution: Battery volts on an output that is off is a shorted switch. Open the master disconnect and do not drive.

do: Before the first drive: the ground offset
how: Meter on DC millivolts between the engine block and the dash ground bus. Engine idling. Then switch on headlights, the defog key and everything else that draws.
expect: Under 50 mV both times
caution: Garage door open.

how: Laptop, USB-to-CAN cable, the limp-home kit with its three fused jumpers, the printed recovery table, beacons. Phone with both apps.
expect: Everything for RC01 to RC10 is in the car

do: Cold start on a cold morning
how: Car left out or in an unheated garage overnight. Take Q-028's reading first if it is still open. Battery app open on the phone. Key to RUN, wait for the pump's 3 s prime, start. Watch the display through the crank, then the battery app as the alternator starts charging.
expect: The display stays up through the crank; the engine starts and the pump holds on; charging rises into 13.8 to 14.6 V. Note what the battery app shows - heater, charge current, temperature: the pack's cold behaviour is not published
caution: A cold lithium pack can refuse charge until its heater has worked. That is the pack protecting itself, not a harness fault.

do: Short first drive, then pull the log
how: A few miles close to home, daylight, dry. Back in the garage, pull the thinned log in the app.
expect: The drive appears in the app; pull time well under a minute

how: After dark: PARK, HEAD, high beam, PASS; watch the pop-ups rise and stay up; each wink with the lights off; every exterior lamp checked by a helper or a reflection; dash illumination and the display's dimming; every tell-tale - turn arrows, high beam, brake, charge.
expect: Every lamp and tell-tale works; the display is readable and not dazzling; no flicker in the headlamps
caution: A headlamp output that latches off raises a warning. If the lamps go out, hazards on and stop.

how: In real rain: wipers LOW, HIGH and INT; switch off mid-sweep and watch them park; WASH held and released. Afterwards look in both footwells and at the dash node for water.
expect: All modes work and park at the bottom; no water near the node, the PMU or any receptacle
caution: Water at the node means a cowl or windscreen leak reaching the electrics. Do not drive in the wet again until its path is fixed.

how: An hour or more, mixed roads, everything used at least once: lights, wipers, defog, head unit, USB charging. Note anything odd with the time it happened.
expect: No warning, no reboot of the display, no output that needed a second try

how: In the app, for each drive: battery voltage (lowest during the crank, highest while charging); global fault, trip state and input faults; CAN health; water temperature and oil pressure; then each output's peak current against its limit - the limits are those entered at E26.
expect: Voltage never above 14.6 V charging; fault channels zero; water under 105 C; oil above its low mark when running; every peak under its limit
caution: A channel whose peak sits at its limit is one that will trip on a cold day. Note it for E32.

how: A note in the app: the two garage readings, the lowest cranking voltage, the highest charging voltage, and any channel whose peak was close to its limit.
expect: Note saved

how: Laptop on DP-DIAG, client connected, engine idling so the lamps see charging voltage. Have the list of outputs in front of you.
expect: Client live; supply voltage in the charging range
caution: Garage door open.

how: One at a time, on for at least two seconds before reading: O6 tail and park - O7 brake - O17 left turn and O18 right turn (read the top of the flash) - O19 reverse - O20 dash illumination at full brightness - O2 low beam - O3 high beam. Write each figure down.
expect: Eight figures; bulbs near their expected amps, the LED headlamps far under

how: O8 wipers LOW and O9 wipers HIGH, on wet glass, mid-sweep. O1 while both pop-ups are travelling, and again while one winks. Write each down.
expect: O8 about 4 A, O9 about 5.5 A; O1 with both moving 8 to 12 A
caution: Hands clear of the arms and the lamp buckets.

how: O4 defog: the reading in the first seconds after switch-on from cold, and again after a minute. O5 fuel pump, engine running. O10 accessory with the head unit on and both USB ports charging. O11 horn, a one-second press. O12 ignition at idle and at 3000 rpm. O21 while cranking and O22 any time: expect zero.
expect: A figure for each; O5 about 2 to 2.4 A; O21 and O22 zero

do: Compare each figure with what was expected
how: More than about 20 percent under: mark the part as tired - a bulb, a motor, the grid. Over the expected figure: stop and find out why before going on.
expect: A short list of tired parts, or none; nothing over

do: Work out the new limits for the lamp outputs
how: Running current x 1.35 for O19 and O20, and check O6, O7, O17 and O18 the same way against the limits they already have. O2 and O3: x 1.35, never above 13.0.
expect: A new limit for each lamp output, none above its pin or its wire

do: Work out the new limits for the others
how: O4 defog, a resistive load: the cold reading x 1.2. O10 accessory, electronics: the loaded reading x 1.5, never above 15. O1 stays at 25.0. O8 and O9: the factor is on stall current, which nobody has measured - leave both at 13.0 and note it. O5 already has a measured limit: leave it. O11, O12, O21, O22: the record does not say which class they are - leave them at their caps and note it.
expect: A new limit for O4 and O10; the rest left with a reason

do: Enter the limits and set the warning bands
how: Type each new Max Current. For each lamp output set Min Current to half its baseline, unless the baseline is under four times the pin's floor - about 0.5 to 2 A on the 25 A pins, 0.2 A on the 15 A pins, 0.1 A on the 7 A pins. For the motor outputs set the over-current warning function at one and a half times the baseline. O21 and O22 get no band.
expect: Limits and bands entered
caution: Min Current only warns. Build no logic on it.

do: Prove every output again from cold
how: Engine off until the bulbs are cold. Then work every output once: lamps, turn signals for a full minute, wipers, pop-ups up and down three times, horn, defog, a start.
expect: Nothing trips; nothing retries; status 1 on everything that is on

how: Save as the next revision to the PMU and the laptop. Replace the file kept with the car's USB-to-CAN cable, so the copy in the glovebox and the one in the module never disagree.
expect: Same revision in three places

how: A note in the app: one line per output with its steady current, plus the list of tired parts.
expect: Note saved

how: Master disconnect OFF. Boots off the battery terminals only when you reach them.
expect: 0 V at the dash busbar
caution: Lithium battery: a tool across the posts welds. One terminal at a time.

how: From the leaflet in each box (or the maker's page): the stud torque of the Class-T block (P047), the MRBF holder (P051), the battery post clamps (P095), the busbar (P007), the PowerPost (P050), the MIDI holders (P053) and the relay sockets' screws. Write part id, which stud, the figure and its unit.
expect: One figure per stud, written down.
caution: These figures are not in the record until you enter them: E8 to E11 torque to them.

do: Set aside anything short or wrong
how: Leave it sealed; photograph label and packing slip; note the row id and the count; contact the seller.
expect: A list of shortfalls, or none.

how: Tick D1; enter shortfalls and the torque figures as notes in the app.
expect: D1 done; D2, D3 and D4 can start.

do: Clear the bench and take metal off your hands
how: Battery on a wooden or plastic surface. Rings and watch off. Keep each post covered until its clamp goes on.
expect: Nothing metal within reach of both posts at once.
caution: Lithium: a tool across the two posts welds, it does not just spark.

how: One of the P095 pair onto the negative post; push it fully down the taper and tighten its pinch bolt.
expect: Clamp cannot be turned by hand.

how: The other P095 clamp onto the positive post, fully down, pinch bolt tight. Cover the negative clamp with its boot while you do it.
expect: Clamp cannot be turned by hand.

do: Load each stud with a 1/0 lug
how: Put one P098 lug (3/8 in hole, uncrimped) on each clamp's 3/8 stud with its washer and nut, as C12 will sit on the positive and C05 on the negative.
expect: Nut fully on with thread showing; the lug lies flat on the clamp.
caution: If the 3/8 hole does not fit the stud, note the stud's size: the lug order is wrong, not the stud.

do: Try the boots over the loaded terminals
how: Red boot on positive, black on negative (P094). Each must cover the clamp, the stud and the lug's barrel end.
expect: No metal visible on either terminal.

do: Lift each boot with one hand
how: Pull each boot off and push it back, one-handed, as you would at the roadside for a jump start.
expect: Each lifts and re-seats without a tool.

do: Try a lug boot on the 1/0 lug
how: Slide a P066 boot over a P098 lug's barrel as it will sit on the cable.
expect: The boot covers the lug's barrel and stud end.

how: Lay the P057 clamp across the case and hang the J-hooks or M8 bolts either side. Check it bears on the case, not on a terminal or a boot.
expect: Clamp spans the 170 mm width or the 230 mm length cleanly; the boots are clear of it.

do: Measure the height over the boots
how: Bench to the top of the fitted boots, in mm.
expect: A figure above 190 mm.

do: Strip it back, tick and note
how: Take the lugs off; leave the clamps on only if both boots stay on. Tick D2 and enter the height as a note.
expect: D2 done.

do: Open the first spare set over a tray
how: Tip the terminals of the first spare 39-way housing into the tray. Keep the two sets apart.
expect: One set in the tray.

how: The large ones fit the 2.8 mm die.
The small ones fit the 1.5 mm die.
Pin 15 takes a medium terminal the record does not name. Note whether the set holds one that is neither large nor small.
expect: Present or absent, written down.

how: Off the housing, the bag or the terminals' carrier strip: the housing's number and each terminal size's number.
expect: Up to three terminal numbers and the housing number written down.

do: Count the second set the same way
how: Large, small, any medium.
expect: 16 and 27 again.

how: "PMU SPARE SET 1" and "SET 2", with the counts on each bag.
expect: Two labelled bags.

how: Tick D3; enter counts and part numbers as a note in the app.
expect: D3 done; D4 may use spare terminals for its test crimps.

how: Hang the scale (P040) from a fixed hook. You will clamp each crimped contact in the vice or locking pliers, tie or loop the wire to the scale's hook, and pull steadily until the scale reads the pass figure. Eye protection on.
expect: Scale reads zero hanging free.
caution: A contact can release suddenly: pull away from your face.

do: Cut and strip three 16 AWG test wires
how: Three 150 mm lengths of 16 AWG GXL (grey P010, or any 16 AWG spool). Strip 6.3 to 7.9 mm (0.250-0.312 in), the length for a size-16 contact [rules crimp; 00-CAR S-502]: the bare strands fill the barrel and show in the inspection hole, and no copper shows behind it.
expect: Clean strands, none cut or nicked.

do: Set the Deutsch crimper for size 16 on 16 AWG
how: P038 is a four-indent crimper for solid contacts. Its selector position and depth for a size-16 contact on 16 AWG are not in the record: use the chart that comes with the tool, and write the setting down.
expect: Setting written down.

do: Crimp three size-16 contacts on 16 AWG
how: Use spares P022 (socket) or P023 (pin). Seat the contact in the crimper, push the stripped wire fully into the barrel, hold the wire in, and close the handles until the ratchet releases.
expect: Four even indents round the barrel; no strand outside it; insulation right up to the barrel.

how: Clamp the contact, hook the wire to the scale and pull steadily to 20 lbf (9.1 kg). Hold a moment.
expect: All three hold at 20 lbf (9.1 kg) or more.
caution: One failure restarts the set of three after a setting change.

do: Size 16 on 14 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Three 14 AWG wires (orange P012). Use the 14 AWG contacts P024 (socket) or P025 (pin), not the 16-18 AWG ones. Reset the crimper per its chart; crimp; pull to 34 lbf (15.4 kg).
expect: All three hold at 34 lbf (15.4 kg).

do: Size 12 on 12 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Three 12 AWG wires (red P015). Contacts P026 (socket) or P027 (pin); there are five of each, so mix them. Strip 5.6 to 7.2 mm (0.222-0.284 in) for a size-12 contact [rules crimp]. Set the crimper for size 12; crimp; pull to 45 lbf (20.4 kg).
expect: All three hold at 45 lbf (20.4 kg).

do: Try the open-barrel dies on one spare PMU terminal
how: Lay a spare small terminal in the 1.5 mm die of P039 and a spare large one in the 2.8 mm die, without wire, and close gently to see the wings roll evenly.
expect: Each terminal sits square in its die.
caution: Spare terminals are the only replacements: one of each for this trial, no more.

do: PMU small terminal on 16 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Spare small terminals from D3's bags, 16 AWG wire, the 1.5 mm die. Strip length: not in the record. Take it from the sheet that comes with the contact or the crimper, strip so the bare strands fill the barrel and no copper shows behind it, and write the length down. Pull to 20 lbf (9.1 kg).
expect: All three hold at 20 lbf (9.1 kg); the wings are rolled into the strands, the rear wings grip the insulation.

do: PMU small terminal on 14 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Six PMU pins (3, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11) carry 14 AWG in a small cavity. Same die; pull to 34 lbf (15.4 kg).
expect: All three hold at 34 lbf (15.4 kg).

do: PMU large terminal on 12 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Spare large terminals, 12 AWG wire, the 2.8 mm die. Pull to 45 lbf (20.4 kg). Pin 25 carries 10 AWG (black P017): crimp one on 10 AWG as well and note what it holds - the record gives no figure for 10 AWG.
expect: Three at 45 lbf (20.4 kg) on 12 AWG; the 10 AWG figure noted.

how: Pin 15 takes a medium terminal whose part and die the record does not name. Do not crimp it by guess: note what D3 found.
expect: Nothing crimped; the gap noted.

how: Offcuts of 2 AWG cable (P061) and lugs P064. Fit the hydraulic crimper P037 with the die for 2 AWG - which die marking fits is not in the record: use the tool's chart and write it down. Strip to the depth of the lug's barrel, push the cable fully home, crimp.
expect: The lug cannot be pulled or twisted off by hand (the record gives no pull figure for a lug - confirm); no strands outside the barrel.
caution: Keep fingers out of the die: a hydraulic crimper does not stop.

do: 1/0 lug: crimp three with the 1/0 dies
how: Offcuts of 1/0 cable (P096) and lugs P098, the 1/0 die pair. Twelve lugs were bought for eight cable ends: three test crimps leave one spare.
expect: The lug cannot be pulled or twisted off by hand; the die closes fully.

do: 6 AWG lug: only if one is spare
how: The alternator cable uses four 6 AWG lugs (P065) and the order's target is four. If more than four arrived, crimp one on a P063 offcut; if not, the first real one at E10 is made with the 2 AWG test's care.
expect: One test lug, or none and a note.

do: Write the settings on the tools
how: For each combination: selector or die, depth, strip length, and the load held. Tape the note inside each crimper's case. Keep the test pieces in a labelled bag.
expect: One line per combination.

how: Tick D4; enter the settings and loads as a note in the app. Any crimper that failed is boxed for return.
expect: D4 done.

do: Lithium: cover both terminals, metal off your hands
how: Whenever the battery is in the car and you are working, both terminals are booted or taped. Rings and watches off.
expect: You can say why: a dropped tool across the posts welds.

do: Open the master disconnect before touching four things
how: The 2 AWG feed, the starter cable, the tank sender, and anything in the pop-up headlamp buckets. Every time. The disconnect is on the POSITIVE side in the cargo bin, so opening it removes supply from everything, the starter cable included.
expect: You can name the four.

do: Before the disconnect is fitted, pull the negative lug
how: Until E9 has fitted the disconnect, the way to make the car dead is to take the negative cable off the battery. Negative comes off first and goes back on last.
expect: You know which cable moves first.

do: Shut the engine down before opening the disconnect
how: The switch has no pole to shut the alternator down first. Engine off, then the switch.
expect: Order known: engine, then switch.
caution: Opening it with the engine running sends the alternator's output into the wiring with no battery to absorb it.

do: Treat every PMU output as possibly live
how: A PMU output's switch fails short, not open: an output can be live with the key out and the module asleep. The only thing that is certainly off is the master disconnect.
expect: You reach for the disconnect, not the key.

do: Keep the unfused cable to inches
how: The cable from the positive post to the disconnect cannot be protected by any fuse. The disconnect and the Class-T block sit as close to the positive post as physically possible.
expect: You know which cable has no fuse.

do: Leave the big fuses out while you build
how: The Class-T fuse (150 A) and the MRBF fuse (250 A) are not fitted until E11. The PMU's first power-up (E24) is through a 5 A fuse bridged across the Class-T block, so a short melts a 5 A fuse and not a 2 AWG cable.
expect: You know when each fuse goes in.

how: Never under the car on a jack alone. Chock the wheels: P on the automatic is not a parking brake.
expect: Stands and chocks by the car.

do: No sparks near the tank; extinguisher within reach
how: The pump and tank sender wiring run under the rear floor to the tank. No grinding, drilling or test sparks near it without looking first. The extinguisher is within reach, not in the next room.
expect: Extinguisher placed.

do: Engine running: clear of belt and fan, garage door open
how: Sleeves and leads clear of the belt, fan and pulleys. Door open: exhaust in a closed garage is carbon monoxide.
expect: Door open before any start.

how: Fingers out of the buckets whenever the motors can be powered. A stalled motor pulls 15 to 25 A.
expect: You open the disconnect before reaching into a bucket.

do: Label the factory end of every migrated circuit
how: When a circuit moves to the new harness, its factory end is labelled MIGRATED with the date and taped back.
expect: Labels and a pen in the kit.
caution: An unlabelled live wire taped behind a dash is the next fault.

do: Label every new wire at both ends the moment it is cut
how: Printed laminated tape, both ends, from / to. Never tape and marker.
expect: You label before cutting the next wire.

do: Torque every heavy connection and paint-mark it
how: Each heavy stud to its maker's figure (read at D1), marked with the paint pen after torquing.
expect: Torque notes and paint pen in the kit.

do: Keep water out of the new parts
how: Every conductor enters the PMU, the dash node and each panel from below or with a drip loop; nothing mounts in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell; the PMU's 39-way connector faces down or sideways, never up.
expect: You can say the three.

do: Never bare aluminium against a live stud; both busbars covered
how: Any aluminium panel is painted or coated; the always-hot busbar and the ground bus both carry covers.
expect: Known.

do: The car does not start, and is not driven, until the list says so
how: It runs at E12 on the new backbone, then does not start from E26 until E28 has moved the last circuit, and is not driven until the interior is back at E35.
expect: Known.

how: Tick E4 in the app.
expect: E4 done; E5 ready.

how: Use one DT06-4S plug kit (P124) that waits on the shelf for a part not fitted this build - L3-RDR's or L4-RDR's. It is the 4-way plug; its wedgelock is W4S. The record buys no spare housing, so treat it gently: it goes back in its bag.
expect: One 4-way plug and its wedgelock on the bench.

how: Two 150 mm lengths of 16 AWG, spare socket contacts P022, crimper P038 at D4's passing setting. Tug each by hand.
expect: Four even indents; neither pulls off by hand.

how: Find the numbers 1 to 4 moulded into the rear (wire side) of the plug.
expect: Cavity 1 found.

how: Take the wedgelock out. Push the contact into cavity 1 from the rear, through the seal, straight, until it clicks.
expect: A click you can feel.
caution: Pushing at an angle tears the rear seal.

how: Pull the wire firmly.
expect: The contact does not back out.

how: Push the wedgelock in from the mating face until it seats.
expect: Wedgelock seated; the contact cannot move.

do: Remove the wedgelock and the contact
how: Pull the wedgelock out with needle-nose pliers. Release the contact with the size-16 removal tool (P031 or P032) as the tool's instructions show, and draw the wire out of the rear.
expect: Contact out undamaged; the seal intact.
caution: Never pull a contact out by force without releasing it: the lock finger breaks.

how: Insert, click, tug, wedgelock, remove - ten times in all, with both removal tools.
expect: It clicks and holds on the tenth as on the first.

how: Join two 16 AWG offcuts with a heat-shrink butt splice (P078) or slide adhesive-lined shrink (P077) over a wire. Heat gun (P042) on its low setting, moving round the joint from the middle outward.
expect: Glue weeps evenly at both ends; no scorching.

how: On a 2 AWG offcut (P061): slide a boot (P066) and a length of heavy-wall adhesive shrink (from P077) on first, crimp a P064 lug with the hydraulic crimper at D4's die, shrink the heavy-wall over the barrel and the first of the insulation, then slide the boot over.
expect: Glue at both ends of the shrink; the boot covers the barrel.
caution: Boot and shrink go on the cable BEFORE the lug: they do not pass over it afterwards.

do: Put the plug kit back in its bag and tick
how: Wedgelock and plug back in the P124 bag, labelled. Tick E5.
expect: E5 done; E6 ready.

how: A TZe-FX231 cartridge (P075, 12 mm black on white, flexible-ID) into the PT-D220 (P041). Batteries or its adapter in.
expect: The printer feeds and cuts.

how: Type TEST / L0-X0 and print one.
expect: A clean 12 mm label.

do: Wrap it on a 16 AWG offcut
how: About 45 mm of label wrapped round the wire with the text outside; rub it down.
expect: The text reads along the wire.

how: A piece of clear 3/16 in heat-shrink (P076) over the label; shrink with the heat gun (P042) on low.
expect: Tube tight, text readable through it.

how: Pull the label along the wire with your fingers.
expect: It does not move.
