do: Get the car and the tools ready
how: Lever in P, handbrake on, wheels chocked, bonnet up, engine cold. Make a page per check in the notepad.
expect: Tools laid out; notepad headed CK19 to CK18.

how: At the engine's rear housing pull the push-on lead (wire BrY) off the oil pressure sender C-09 - it is the upper one; the water temperature sender is directly below. Meter on ohms, one probe on the sender's terminal, one on the engine block.
expect: Open circuit at 0 psi (the 1985 figure).

how: Leave the lead off the sender. Start the engine and let it warm. At idle, read ohms from the sender's terminal to the block. Then stop the engine and push the lead back on.
expect: A resistance that falls as pressure rises; the 1985 book gives about 197 ohm at the first mark and 141 ohm at 60 psi.
caution: Belt and fan are turning: sleeves and leads clear. Garage door open.

how: At the hatch release switch's plug on the dash (wires LR and GR) and the fuel-door switch's plug (LR and GB): unplug the switch and bridge LR to the other wire through the ammeter for half a second. LR is live with the key out. Or use the clamp meter round the GR or GB wire while you press the switch.
expect: The hatch pops, then the fuel door; a current for each in amps. Unknown: the factory fuse is 20 A.
caution: Use the 20 A range or the clamp, half a second only: an unknown current can blow a meter's 10 A fuse.

how: At the hatch glass, part the grid's two connections (wire LG in, wire B to ground). Ohms across the grid. Then feed 12 V to the LG tab through the fused lead with the B tab on ground, put the meter's black probe on the B tab and slide the red probe along each line.
expect: About 1 ohm across the grid if the design's 10 to 13 A is right (arithmetic; nothing has been measured). Along a good line the volts fall evenly from 12 to 0; a jump marks a break.
caution: The grid is peeling: touch the lines lightly. Expect 10 to 13 A; fuse the lead at 15 A.

how: Fill the reservoir. At the pump's plug D-01, on the pump side: 12 V from the fused lead to the LB terminal, a jumper from the LY terminal to ground.
expect: It runs and sprays, or it does not. If it runs, the fault is in the car's circuit, not the pump.

do: CK23: which wire is low beam
how: Raise both lamps with the manual knobs on the motors. Unplug the left lamp (E-08: RY, RL, B). On the lamp side put the B terminal to ground, then 12 V from the fused lead on RY alone, then on RL alone. Note which beam lights each time. Repeat on the right lamp (E-09).
expect: RY lights low beam, RL lights high beam.

how: Battery negative off. With calipers and a thread gauge (or a known nut) measure the thread of: the alternator's B stud, the starter's B and S terminals, any stud on the two battery clamps, and the PMU's stud (the manual says M6). Then read the part numbers on the spare PMU terminals in hand, the 1.5 mm and the 2.8 mm.
expect: A diameter and pitch for each stud; terminal numbers (the pinout lists 211CC2S2160P, 211CC3S2120 and 211CC3S3120).
caution: The alternator B stud and the starter B terminal are live until the battery negative is off.

do: CK08: ohm the left pop-up motor, parked
how: Battery negative still off. Unplug the left motor's four-way plug E-03 (YG top, WR left, RY right, R bottom). On the motor side, with the lamp parked, read ohms for: WR to case, R to case, RY to case, YG to case, WR to R, WR to RY, R to RY.
expect: Seven readings. Write 'open' where the meter shows nothing.

do: CK08: the same half-raised and raised
how: Turn the motor's manual knob until the lamp is half up and take the seven readings again; then fully up, and again.
expect: Twenty-one readings for the left motor.

how: The same on plug E-04: seven readings parked, half-raised and raised.
expect: Twenty-one readings for the right motor.

how: Battery negative back on. One motor at a time, on the motor side of its plug: 12 V from the fused lead to WR and a jumper from the motor's case to ground. Touch a second 12 V lead to R alone: note which way the lamp moves and whether it stops by itself. Take it off. Touch it to RY alone: note the same. While the motor runs, read the volts on YG.
expect: R raises the lamp and it stops at the top; RY lowers it and it stops at the bottom; YG shows about 12 V only while it moves.
caution: Hands and leads out of the bucket and the linkage. If the motor does not stop within a few seconds, take the 12 V off. The record gives no fuse size for this test: start with a small fuse and go up only if it blows on starting.

how: Put the ammeter in the WR feed. Read the current with the motor stopped on its cam and the same command still applied (12 V left on R with the lamp already up). Then read it while the lamp travels. Do both motors.
expect: Two figures per motor: stopped (idle) and travelling. They set the pop-up cycle's current threshold.

how: Battery negative off. Unplug the wiper motor's four-way D-02 and its single B plug. On the motor side, arms parked, read ohms: L to case, LB to case, L to LB, L to LW, L to LR, B to case. Then replug, battery on, run the wipers and switch the key off when the arms are mid-screen; battery negative off, unplug, and take the six readings again.
expect: Twelve readings. The record expects LB joined to L at park and to B away from park, and B joined to the case.

how: Arms lifted off the glass or the glass wet. On the motor side: 12 V from the fused lead on LW, and L to ground. Note whether it runs.
expect: It runs, or it does not - either is the answer.
caution: The arms sweep: keep clear.

do: CK10: does IG hold through START
how: Plugs back on, battery on, lever in P. Meter on DC volts, black probe on a good ground, red probe on the ignition switch's IG wire. The diagram colours it BY, and the START wire may be BY as well: IG is the one that goes live at RUN. Turn the key OFF, ACC, RUN, then hold START. If the switch's wires cannot be reached with the column covers on, do this straight after the next step.
expect: About 12 V at RUN that stays there while the key is held at START.
caution: The engine cranks and may start. Lever in P, nobody in front of the car.

how: The steering column's upper and lower covers. The screws are not in the record: bag and label them as you find them.
expect: The backs of the stalk switches and their plugs in view.

do: CK17: the light switch's contact table
how: Battery negative off. Unplug the light switch's two plugs E-01 (2-pin: R, WG; 6-pin: RG, RW, R, RL, RY, GL). On the switch side, with the meter on continuity, find every pair of terminals that is joined - in OFF, PARK, HEAD low and HEAD high, each once with the stalk released and once pulled to PASS.
expect: A table of joined pairs for eight cases. The 1980 table shows PASS closing the same contact as HIGH, not one of its own.
caution: R and WG are live with the key out until the battery is off.

do: CK18: the turn and hazard switch
how: Unplug F-02 (WG, GY, GW, GB, GR, GO). On the switch side find every joined pair with the stalk LEFT, in neutral, RIGHT, and with the hazard switch ON.
expect: A table for four cases. The 1980 table shows no contact to ground at OFF and three terminals joined by the hazard switch.

how: Unplug D-03 (B, LO, LY, LR, LG, LW). Find every joined pair in OFF, INT, LOW, HIGH, and with the washer pressed.
expect: A table for five cases.

do: Put it back as it was
how: Refit every plug until it latches. Battery negative on. Check the lights, the stalks and the wipers work as before. Leave the column covers off if the strip (S1) follows; bag their screws.
expect: The car works as it did this morning.

how: Tick V-114 and type each check's readings, starting each block with its number.
expect: Eleven blocks of readings in the app.

how: Bonnet up, engine cold, key out. Torch, camera, ruler, tape and pen to hand. Nothing in this row is unbolted or unplugged.
caution: The battery is live. Keep the ruler and spanners away from its posts.

how: Follow the battery's positive cable. Near the battery is a small block holding three short lengths of soft wire: one black (the main link, 1.25 sq) with a brown one (0.3 sq) either side. Photograph it with the ruler. Write: where it is fastened, how its battery side is joined (a ring on the battery clamp, a wire into the positive cable, a plug), that wire's colour, and the colours of the wires leaving it.
expect: One black link between two brown ones; a white wire with a red stripe (WR) leaving the black one - by the diagram, confirm.

do: Measure from the block to the starter and to the bulkhead
how: With the tape, along the way a wire would run: from the block's battery side to the starter's large stud, and from the block to the nearest bulkhead grommet. Write both in mm.
expect: Two lengths. They decide where the block is fed from once the battery has moved to the back.

how: From the negative post to every place it lands: the body, the engine or gearbox, or both. At each end note what it bolts to and try a spanner on the bolt for size. Look for a second, smaller lead from the same clamp. Photograph each end.
expect: The diagram shows one cable to ground and does not say where; one or two ends, read off the car.

do: Look at the alternator's output stud
how: The large stud on the back of the alternator, usually under a rubber boot. Without undoing it: how many ring terminals are on it, each wire's colour and rough thickness, and the nut's spanner size. Photograph it.
expect: One ring with a white / red (WR) wire - by the diagram, confirm.
caution: This stud is live with the battery connected. Do not touch it with a tool.

do: Look at the starter's large stud and the space beside it
how: On the starter solenoid: what is on the large stud (the battery cable and anything else), and the small terminal's wire colour. Then find a flat place near it where the two bolt-down fuse holders (F17 and F18) could be fixed side by side: say where it is and how far from the stud in mm. Photograph both.
expect: The battery cable on the large stud; a black / white (BW) wire on the small terminal - by the record, confirm.
caution: Live stud, as the alternator's.

do: Find bolts for the engine-to-body strap
how: On the engine block or its front cover: a threaded boss with nothing in it, or a bolt that could take a cable lug under its head. On the body or chassis rail within 610 mm of it along the path a cable would take: a bolt or a place for one on solid metal. Try a spanner on each for size, measure the distance between the two, photograph both.
expect: One pair of points 610 mm apart or less. A second boss on the block for the heavy return cable from the rear, if there is one.

do: Pick the place for the front star stud
how: On the radiator support: a flat of solid metal reachable from above, clear of the radiator and the bonnet latch, where a 3/8 in stud can go through and be reached from behind for its nut. Then a second existing body bolt close by for its bond wire. Photograph both with the ruler and note the bolt's spanner size.

X-13: on the left suspension tower, a bolt with one or more black wires under it. X-14: its place is not in the record - follow the black wire back from the right headlamp. X-15: its place is not in the record either - follow the black wires from the tail lamps and the fuel pump. For each: where it is, how many wires, and whether the metal under it is clean, painted or rusty. Photograph each.
expect: Three points. X-13 and X-15 are the two the turn-signal fault was traced to on paper; rust or paint under a terminal is the finding.

do: Pick the place for the rear ground stud
how: In the cargo bin where V-088's cardboard battery sits: solid metal - a seam, a rail or a bracket, not a thin floor skin - within reach of the battery's negative post. Check what is on the other side of that metal and whether a nut could be reached there. Then a second bolt nearby for its bond wire. Measure from the spot to where the negative post will be, photograph it with the ruler.
expect: A spot about 900 mm or less from the negative post - the cable is estimated at 3 ft, confirm.
caution: Whatever is behind that panel - a tank, a line, wiring - is found before any hole is ever drilled. Today only look.

do: LOOK: the plugs in the engine bay
how:
Part nothing: the car must still run for V-114. Count the wires going into each housing, note the housing's colour and any maker's name or number moulded into it, say whether it is a housing on a pigtail or a terminal pushed straight onto the part, and whether it is sound, cracked or cut about. One photo of each with the ruler beside it. The coils and igniters are on the upper rear housing, the alternator's small plug at its back, the two senders one above the other at the rear housing, the brake-fluid switch in the reservoir cap. The inhibitor switch and the kick-down solenoid are on the transmission: if neither can be seen from above, say so - C1 looks at them from under the car.
DV01 Coils + igniters: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Igniters B-20 and B-21: factory connector, 2 wires each on the diagram (YG, BW and YL, BW). Coils B-18 and B-19: one single-way connector each (YG, YL) plus a ring terminal for BW; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV02 Starter: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Main B stud for a ring lug, plus the S terminal on factory connector A-01, 1 wire on the diagram (BW on an automatic); the stud thread, and whether A-01 is a bare push-on terminal or a 1-way housing: not known - confirm
DV04 Alternator: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory 2-way coupler A-08 on the regulator, 2 wires on the diagram (BW, WB), plus the B output A-09 drawn as a ring terminal (WR); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV05 Inhibitor switch: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector A-06, 4 wires on the diagram (BY, GY over BW, RW); whether the switch carries a lead of its own, housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV06 Water temp sender: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Single terminal on the sender, 1 wire on the diagram (YW): the devices row calls it a spade, the diagram draws a single-way connector; terminal size: not known - confirm
DV07 Oil pressure sender: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Single terminal on the sender, 1 wire on the diagram (BrY): the devices row calls it a spade, the diagram draws a single-way connector; terminal size: not known - confirm
DV08 Brake fluid level switch: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector C-05, 2 wires on the diagram (BR, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV51 Kick-down solenoid: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - B-33: one single-way connector on the diagram (BR); the return is through the transmission case. Whether a bare push-on terminal or a 1-way housing, and which half is on the solenoid: not known - confirm
expect: Eight lines for the plug list, each with a photo or the words 'not seen from above'.
caution: The alternator's and the starter's large studs are live. Look, do not touch them with the ruler.

do: LOOK: the plugs at the nose and the cowl
how:
Part nothing: the car must still run for V-114. Count the wires going into each housing, note the housing's colour and any maker's name or number moulded into it, say whether it is a housing on a pigtail or a terminal pushed straight onto the part, and whether it is sound, cracked or cut about. One photo of each with the ruler beside it. Raise the headlamps with the switch and look behind each bucket for the lamp's plug and the motor's; the front combination lamps and side markers from behind the bumper and inside the wings; the horns behind the bumper; the wiper motor and the washer pump at the cowl.
DV10 Headlights: the record has, from the maker's sheet - The Grote 94401-5 LED unit (luxury LP41) has an H4 connection, 3-pin by Grote's family sheet, and comes with an adapter block for 2E1-style harnesses. The factory lamp connector E-08 / E-09 has 3 wires on the diagram (RL, RY, B); whether that socket mates the H4 connection: not known - confirm
DV11 Pop-up motors: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector E-03 / E-04, 4 wires on the diagram (YG, WR, RY, R), drawn as four round terminals in a cross; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV12 Front combo lamps: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector F-05 / F-06, 3 wires on the diagram (RG, GR or GO, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known. The LED bulbs (luxury LP53) go in the lamp's own bulb holder, so the plug does not change - confirm
DV13 Front side markers: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector F-12 / F-13, 2 wires on the diagram (B, RG); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known. The LED bulb (luxury LP53) goes in the lamp's own holder - confirm
DV14 Horns: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Single terminal per horn, 1 wire on the diagram (GY), labelled a single spade in 00-CAR's terminals rows; the case grounds through the bracket. Terminal size: not known - confirm
DV15 Wiper motor: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector D-02, 4 wires on the diagram (LW, LR over L, LB), plus a separate single-way connector for B; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV16 Washer pump: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector D-01, 2 wires on the diagram (LY, LB); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: Seven lines for the plug list.
caution: Hands out of the headlamp buckets while the switch is worked: the lamps move fast. Switch off and take the key out before reaching in.

do: LOOK: the plugs at the rear
how:
Part nothing: the car must still run for V-114. Count the wires going into each housing, note the housing's colour and any maker's name or number moulded into it, say whether it is a housing on a pigtail or a terminal pushed straight onto the part, and whether it is sound, cracked or cut about. One photo of each with the ruler beside it. From the cargo area and the open hatch: the two tabs of the defogger grid on the hatch glass, the tail lamps' plugs behind the rear trim if they can be reached without taking it off, the licence lamps and rear markers, the luggage lamp and its switch, the hatch-release solenoid at the latch, the fuel-door solenoid behind the driver-side quarter trim. The fuel pump and the tank sender are under the floor: look only if they can be seen without lifting the car, and read the pump's maker and number off its body if you can.
DV33 Rear defog grid: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - G-25: two single-way connectors on the diagram, one per side of the grid (LG, B), drawn in two different shapes; whether they are tabs on the glass, and their size: not known - confirm
DV34 Fuel pump: the record has, from the maker's sheet - Two terminals on the pump for two terminal wires; Carter's sheet draws both a screw-type and a push-on-type terminal and does not say which the P4070 has. Which pump is on the car is itself still to be read off it - confirm
DV36 Fuel level sender: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector C-01, 2 wires on the diagram (B, Y); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV37 Rear combo lamps: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector F-07 / F-08, a 6-cavity housing with 5 wires on the diagram (GR or GO, RW, one not used, over G, RG, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV38 Licence lamps + rear markers: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - F-04 licence lamps: two single-way connectors per lamp on the diagram (RG, B). F-14 / F-15 rear markers: 2-way connector, 2 wires (B, RG); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV40 Luggage lamp: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - H-11 lamp: two single-way connectors on the diagram (LY, RB). H-12 lid switch: one single-way connector (RB), closing to body ground; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV48 Hatch-release solenoid: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector H-14, 2 wires on the diagram (GR, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV49 Fuel-door release solenoid: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector H-16, 2 wires on the diagram (GB, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: Eight lines for the plug list, each with a photo or the words 'behind trim, not seen' - those are looked at when S1 has the trim out.
caution: Do not scrape the defogger tabs or flex the glass. No test lead or spark near the tank.

how: Tick V-115 in the app. In the answer type one line per step, 2 to 10: what is there, the wire colours, the spanner sizes, the distances in mm. Then the plug list, one line per device id.

do: Check the list is clear, write down the odometer, photograph the whole interior
how: In the app S1 must be ready and V-114 answered. Read the odometer and write it on the first page of the notepad and in the app. Then, before anything moves: wide shots of the dash, the console, each footwell, each door opening, both seats and the cargo area. These show how it goes back.
expect: S1 ready; the odometer noted; a dozen wide photos.

how: The lead-acid battery is in its factory place in the engine bay. Lift the negative clamp off its post and tuck it clear.
expect: No dome light, no clock.
caution: Do this before any plug is parted.

do: Set up the bags, the labels and the plug list
how: One bag per panel, the panel's name written on it, its fasteners inside. For plugs: tear two tape flags, write the same code on both - the diagram code if you know it (X-05, H-13), otherwise a running number - and put one on each half before you part them. Start a page in the notepad headed PLUGS, one line per device id, for the three steps below marked LOOK. At each: with the two halves apart - or as it sits, if it will not part - count the cavities and the wires, note the housing's colour and any maker's name or number moulded into it, and say which half is on the part (bare pins or blades on the part, or a housing on a pigtail). Photograph the face square-on with the ruler beside it, and once from the side.
expect: Bags, tape, marker and the PLUGS page within reach of the car.

how: Each seat rides on two slide adjusters bolted to the floor. Slide the seat to reach the front bolts, then the rear ones. Before lifting, look for a wire to the driver's belt buckle (Br and BrW) and unplug it, labelled. Lift each seat out with a helper. Bag the bolts as SEAT LEFT and SEAT RIGHT and note the socket size.
expect: Both seats out; four bolts or more per seat bagged - the count is not in the record.
caution: A seat is heavy and awkward: two people, and mind the door sills and the paint.

do: Take off the shift knob and the indicator panel
how: The knob unscrews from the lever against its lock nut. Lift the shift position indicator panel and unplug its lamp (plug E-07), labelled.
expect: Knob and panel off; one lamp plug labelled.
caution: Count how many turns the knob takes to come off: its depth sets the P and N interlock when it goes back.

how: The box between the seats with its lid. It sits on a rear bracket and a centre-rear bracket. Where its screws are is not in the record: look inside the box first. Lift it out and bag them as REAR CONSOLE.
expect: Rear console out.

do: Take off the handbrake lever covers and the front console
how: The lever has a left and a right cover with a ring. The front console sits on a front and a centre bracket; the catalogue lists four console caps, so look under them for screws. Unplug anything in it - the mirror switch or the coin box's panel - labelled. Bag as FRONT CONSOLE.
expect: The tunnel bare from the dash to the rear bulkhead.
caution: Leave the handbrake cable and its switch wire (BR) alone.

do: Photograph behind the dash before anything is unplugged
how: Lie in each footwell with the torch. Photograph the fuse block, every plug, every bundle and where it is clipped, and the backs of the switches. Wide first, then close enough to read wire colours. Save under dash.
expect: Every plug behind the dash in at least one sharp photo.

do: Take off the steering column covers
how: If they are not already off from V-114: the upper and lower covers come apart round the column. The stalk switches stay on the column and stay plugged in. The 1985 drawing takes the horn cap, nut and steering wheel off first; do that only if the 1982 covers will not clear the wheel, and mark the wheel and the shaft first.
expect: Column bare, switches still plugged.
caution: If the wheel comes off, its nut goes back at 40-50 N-m.

do: LOOK: the plugs of the column switches
how:
Under the bare column, where each switch's lead meets the dash harness. Part each plug only if it comes apart easily, look, and plug it back: these switches stay on the column. The ignition switch gets a new electrical portion later, so its plug matters most: count it twice.
DV18 Ignition switch: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Not picked (01-electrical P086, not carted), so its plug cannot be known until it is. The factory switch is on X-08, drawn as two 2-way connectors (WR, BW and BY, L), with the start lead on X-09 (BY, through the 0.5 sq fusible link) - confirm
DV19 Light switch: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector E-01 in two parts on the diagram: a 2-way (R, WG) and a 6-way (RW, R, GL over RL, RY, RG); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV20 Turn stalk: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector F-02, an 8-cavity housing with 6 wires on the diagram (WG, GW, GY, GR over two not used, GO, GB), shared with the hazard switch DV21; housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV21 Hazard switch: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - No plug of its own: the hazard section shares factory connector F-02 with the turn stalk DV20 (8 cavities, 6 wires on the diagram); which cavities are the hazard contact's is read off the diagram, not the car - confirm
DV22 Wiper stalk: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory connector D-03, 6 wires on the diagram (B, LO, LY over LR, LG, LW); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV23 Horn pad: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - No plug of its own on the diagram: the horn contact leaves the column as the GL cavity of the E-01 6-way connector (DV19) and returns through the column; how the pad itself connects at the wheel: not known - confirm
expect: Six lines on the PLUGS page and a photo of each plug face against the ruler.
caution: The battery negative is off: nothing here is live. Do not pull on the horn pad's wire at the wheel.

how: The lid, then the compartment, then the side panel beside it. Unplug the glovebox lamp (H-01) and its lid switch (H-02: wire BL and a ring terminal to ground), labelled. Bag as GLOVEBOX.
expect: The passenger side open to the firewall.

do: Take off the driver's lower switch panel
how: The panel under the dash on the driver's side. Unplug each dash switch as it comes into reach, here and beside the cluster, and label both halves with its 1982 code: headlamp retractor E-02, rear defrost G-24, hatch release H-13 (wires LR, GR), fuel-door release H-15 (wires LR, GB). Which panel each switch sits in is not in the record. Bag as LOWER PANEL LEFT.
expect: Panel off; four switch plugs labelled, or as many as this car has.

do: LOOK: the plugs at the pedals
how:
With the lower panel off, at the pedal box: the stop-lamp switch on the brake pedal bracket and the kick-down switch at the throttle pedal. Both stay where they are and stay plugged in.
DV25 Brake pedal switch: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Not picked (01-electrical P085, any 2-terminal type, Standard SLS-52 class, not carted), so its plug cannot be known until it is. The factory switch F-11 has a 2-way connector, 2 wires on the diagram (GW, W) - confirm
DV50 Kick-down switch: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - B-32: two single-way connectors on the diagram (BW, BR), one per terminal; whether bare push-on terminals or 1-way housings, and which half is on the switch: not known - confirm
expect: Two lines on the PLUGS page and two photos.

do: Take out the radio and the amplifier
how: If it is the factory radio its knobs pull off and nuts on the shafts hold it (1980 manual, another car - confirm); an aftermarket head unit comes out its own way. Draw it forward. Unplug its harness plug (G-04), the aerial lead and the lead to the amplifier, labelled; note where its earth wire bolts. The factory amplifier (plug G-08) is expected behind it: unplug it and take it out with the radio. How these are joined to the car's wiring is V-116's look, after this row.
expect: Radio and amplifier on the bench, their plugs labelled.

do: Take out the clock, the lighter and the ash tray
how: Clock: one four-way plug (H-10). Lighter: plug H-09 (wires LY, RL, B). Slide the ash tray out. Label and bag.
expect: Three more pieces out.

how: Pull its knobs. Unplug the fan switch (G-15) and the panel's lamp, labelled. The mode and temperature levers work the heater through control cables: mark each cable and the lever position it was in, then unclip it at whichever end is easier. Bag the clips as HEATER CONTROLS.
expect: The control panel free of the dash, its cables marked.
caution: Do not kink the control cables, and do not touch any A/C pipe.

how: The surround that held the radio and the heater controls. Find its screws - some may only show now the radio is out - and lift it away. Bag as CENTRE PANEL.
expect: The centre stack open: you can see the heater unit and the tunnel.

do: LOOK: the plugs at the centre stack, the console and the glovebox
how:
Now that they are in the open: the handbrake switch at the lever, the blower motor's plug at the heater case, the three panel lamps (heater panel, gear-lever surround, switch panel) and the glovebox lamp with its lid switch.
DV26 Parking brake switch: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - Factory single-way connector C-04, 1 wire on the diagram (BR); the switch grounds through its body. Whether it is a bare push-on terminal or a 1-way housing, and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV27 Blower motor: the record has, from our own design - New motor, Four Seasons 35483 class, 2 wires; the maker's own connector is not known (one search found no sheet). The leg ends in our Deutsch DTP04-2P receptacle and the motor's lead takes the DTP06-2S plug - confirm the motor's lead; housing L3-BLW
DV30 Dash illumination lamps: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - E-06 heater panel: 2-way connector, 2 wires on the diagram (RL, B). E-07 select lever: two single-way connectors (RL, B). E-10 switch panel: drawn as a bulb socket with 2 wires (RL, B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
DV31 Glove box lamp: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - H-01 lamp: drawn as a bulb socket with 2 wires on the diagram (LO, BL). H-02 lid switch: one single-way connector (BL) and a ring terminal (B); housing style, colour and which half is on the part: not known - confirm
expect: Four lines on the PLUGS page - one per device, the lamps of one device on one line - and a photo of each.

how: Take off the meter hood (two springs hold it) and any switch panels beside the cluster, unplugging and labelling their switches. Undo the cluster, draw it forward, reach behind and release the speedometer cable, then unplug the two round 13-cavity connectors, labelled X-05 and X-06. Store the cluster face up in a box.
expect: The cluster out with both plugs labelled; the binnacle is an open hole.
caution: Do not force the round plugs: look how they lock before pulling. The cluster goes back in for the first start.

how: The defroster grilles, the garnish along the windscreen (three caps cover its screws), the two side garnishes and the vent louvres. Bag as DASH TOP.
expect: Dash-top screws exposed.

how: The 1985 drawing lists a pair of bolts and a set of four for the panel, and the catalogue shows a bracket right and left; find this car's. Before it moves, unclip the dash harness from the panel wherever it is tied to it, so the harness stays in the car. With a helper lift the panel back and out through a door. Bag as DASH. No opening is measured first: the panel is rebuilt around the new units.
expect: The dash on a blanket; the dash harness, the heater unit and the pedals all still in the car and connected.
caution: The harness stays: if a wire comes with the panel, stop and unclip it. Do not open any A/C line.

do: Take out the kick panels and the sill plates
how: The trim panel in front of each door and the plate along each door sill. Bag as KICK LEFT, KICK RIGHT, SILL LEFT, SILL RIGHT.
expect: The sills and the lower A-pillars bare.

how: Roll it out in its pieces. If a seat-belt anchor traps it, undo the anchor and bag the bolt (it goes back at 39-55 N-m). Store the carpet flat and dry.
expect: Bare floor, front to back; any loom lying on the floor now visible.

do: Open the cargo bins, and LOOK at the roof lamp's plug
how:
Take out the cargo floor covering and the trim and lids of both storage bins behind the seats. Leave the luggage lamp and its wiring where they are; the rear lamps', the pump's and the releases' plugs are V-115's looks. Then the interior lamp on the roof rail: ease its lens or housing down far enough to see how its wires join.
DV39 Interior / spot lamp: the record has, from the 1982 wiring diagram - H-06 on the mirror assembly: two single-way connectors on the diagram (LY, RY), read as bullet terminals in 00-CAR's terminals rows; no ground wire is drawn. Which half is on the lamp: not known - confirm
expect: Both bins open and empty; one more line on the PLUGS page.

do: Photograph the looms and the removed pieces, check the work and enter it
how: Now everything is in view: every connector, every splice, every clip and bracket, and the ground points (X-13 at the front of the cabin, X-15 at the rear). Previous-owner splices and the wideband gauge's tap go under hacks. Wide first, then close. Then, for the car model, the dash, the binnacle, the console, the kick panels and the sill plates, each laid flat with the ruler beside it. Walk round: every parted plug has the same label on both halves; nothing is cut; every bag is labelled and in one box. Then tick S1 in the app with the odometer reading, what you found, and the PLUGS page typed in, one line per device id.
expect: A photo of every plug and every length of loom, filed by zone; S1 ticked. The measurement day (C1) opens.

how: Do Q-014 first, from its own steps: the dash post's place depends on it.
expect: Q-014 answered.

how: With the dash out look at the cowl seam, both lower corners of the windscreen and the heater case's drain, and follow the path each would take to the footwell. Look for old water marks and rust trails. Photograph both sides.
expect: A sentence and a photo for the left side and for the right.
caution: Anything that would run onto the dash node moves the node, not the water.

how: From Q-014's spaces choose where the four legs will plug in: low, near the centre stack, not in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell and not under a water path. Put a tape cross there and write DASH POST on it.
expect: A marked point every dash run starts from.

how: Tape the end of the string at the 'from' point. Lay it along the exact path the wires will take, through the grommet named, round every corner, to the 'to' point, and pinch it there. Pull it out and measure it against the tape. Write the length in feet to one decimal beside the run's number.
expect: A number in feet for the run.

how: RT01 dash post to the engine-bay junction, through the firewall grommet on the passenger side. Mark where the leg will fan out in the bay: that is the junction. RT02 junction to the coils and igniters, along the upper rear housing. RT03 junction to the alternator, down the front of the block. RT04 junction to the water temperature and oil pressure senders at the rear housing. RT05 junction to the starter, the start relay's place on the inner fender and the inhibitor switch, under the intake. RT26 junction to the brake fluid switch, along the firewall to the reservoir.
expect: Six lengths.
caution: Engine cold.

how: RT06 dash post to the nose splice, through the cowl grommet and along the inner wing - the longest front run. RT07 nose splice to one headlamp bucket and its pop-up motor, across the radiator support. RT08 nose splice to the front lamps, side markers and horns, along the radiator support and both inner wings. RT09 nose splice back along the cowl to the wiper motor and the washer pump. RT29 nose splice to the front bumper, along the bumper beam.
expect: Five lengths; the model guessed 11.4, 3.4 and 6.1 ft for the first three.

how: RT10 dash post to the steering column, behind the lower dash. RT11 dash post to the centre stack, across the dash rail. RT12 dash post to the glovebox, across the dash rail on the passenger side. RT13 dash post up to the binnacle, behind the cluster opening. RT14 dash post down the centre to the heater case and the pedal box. RT22 dash post along the dash rail to the two spare receptacles behind the dash. RT27 centre stack to under the driver's seat, down the tunnel side and under the carpet line. RT28 the same to under the passenger seat.
expect: Eight lengths. RT11 should be short: it proves the node is close to the centre stack.

do: Measure the rear leg, L4, forward part
how: RT15 dash post to the rear node in the cargo bin, through the tunnel. RT21 dash post to the transmission's speedometer drive and the kick-down solenoid, through the tunnel with RT15. RT19 dash post to the sill node behind the driver's kick panel, along the sill. RT20 sill node to each door, through the door jamb boot.
expect: Four lengths; the model guessed 7.7 ft for the tunnel, 3.8 for the sill, 7.5 for a door.

do: Measure the tunnel for the whole bundle
how: Along RT15's path find the tightest place. Measure the free width and height there in mm. It has to pass the rear leg's bundle, one 2 AWG cable and two 1/0 cables together.
expect: A width x height in mm and where the tight place is.

do: Measure the rear leg, L4, rear part
how: From the rear node: RT16 to the tail lamps, licence lamps and rear markers, along the quarter on both sides. RT17 to the fuel pump and the tank sender, under the floor to the tank. RT18 to the hatch release and the luggage lamp, through the hatch hinge loop - hatch open. RT23 up the C-pillar to the roof-rail interior lamp. RT24 to the defogger grid on the hatch glass, through the hinge loop. RT25 to the fuel-door solenoid behind the driver-side quarter trim.
expect: Six lengths; the model guessed 9.1 ft for the tail lamps and 7.8 for the hatch.
caution: No sparks or test leads near the tank.

how: RT30 centre stack to the amplifier's place in the passenger-side cargo bin, along the passenger sill. RT31 passenger-side bin to the driver-side bin, across the cargo floor behind the seats. RT32 from the passenger-side bin forward along both sills to the front kick panels and the A-pillar bases, up the tunnel side to the console, and to the rear quarters.
expect: Three lengths; for RT32 write each branch.

how: The same way, with string: C03 from the Class-T fuse's place in the passenger-side bin through the tunnel to the dash post; C04 from the same bin to the starter's B terminal; C11 from the rear ground stud's place to the engine block; C07 from the alternator's B stud to the starter's B terminal.
expect: Four lengths in feet, to set against the guesses of 16, 18, 18 and 4 ft.

how: Under the car, at the transmission: unscrew the speedometer cable from its drive boss. Measure the boss thread's diameter with calipers and its pitch with the gauge, and note what the cable's end engages inside. Screw the cable back. While you are under there, the two plugs V-115 could not see from above, if it left them: the inhibitor switch's and the kick-down solenoid's, on the transmission - count the wires, note the housing's colour and any mark, photograph each, and add the two lines to V-115's plug list.
expect: A diameter and pitch in mm, and a word on the drive.
caution: Jack stands under the car, wheels chocked. Never under a car on a jack alone.

do: Count the pins on the used-only parts
how: Count the terminals and photograph the plug face of: the wiper motor (the diagram shows a four-way and a single), each pop-up motor (four), the fuel tank sender (two).
expect: Four counts and four photos.

how: In this order, each from its own steps: V-055 the sill, A5 the wire colours, Q-115 the speedometer head, V-112 the releases, V-116 the head unit and wideband taps, V-081 the pop-ups. V-088 and V-115 were taken with the car whole: check each is answered.
expect: Each row answered in the app.

how: Anything uncovered today that S1's photos missed: the grommets, the tunnel, the bins, the rear ground point X-15.
expect: Photos filed by zone.

how: Tick C1 and type the 32 run lengths, the four cable lengths, the tunnel gap, the pin counts, the boss thread and the CK04 sentences.
expect: C1 ticked. The agent works the wire order out from your numbers.

do: Lay out what S1 took out
how: The head unit and the amplifier are out of the dash from S1, still on their wires where the wires allow, or unplugged at their own plugs with labels on. Battery negative stays off. Torch, camera, tape and pen to hand.
caution: Cut nothing and strip no tape from the factory loom.

do: Trace the head unit's power wires
how: One at a time: red (ACC), yellow (battery), orange (illumination), black (ground). Follow each from the head unit's plug to where it joins the car. Write the car-side wire's colour and how the two are joined: a plug adaptor into the factory radio plug, a crimp, twisted and taped, or a tap connector. Label the joint with the head unit wire's colour and photograph it.
expect: Four joints, or an adaptor plug carrying all four.

do: Note any fuse in the head unit's wires
how: An inline holder in the red or yellow wire, or a fuse on the back of the unit: write its rating.

Its heavy power wire: where it gets its supply (the battery, the fuse block, a tap) and the fuse in it. Its ground: which bolt. The thin blue / white remote wire from the head unit. The speaker wires: whether they go into the factory speaker wiring or are their own runs. Label and photograph each end.

Find the gauge and follow its harness. The +12 V wire: where it taps the car (a wire colour, a fuse-block tap) and whether it has its own fuse. The ground: which bolt or wire. The lead ending in a small 2-way plug (AEMnet): plugged into anything, or loose. The sensor lead: which grommet it leaves the cabin by. Label and photograph each.

do: Look for anything else that is not factory
how: Along the loom behind the dash and down both footwells: an alarm or immobiliser box, a kill switch, added relays, tap connectors, wires in colours the loom does not use. For each: photograph it, label it, and follow it one joint in each direction.

do: LOOK: the plugs at the radio opening and on the gauge
how:
At each: with the two halves apart - or as it sits, if it will not part - count the cavities and the wires, note the housing's colour and any maker's name or number moulded into it, and say which half is on the part (bare pins or blades on the part, or a housing on a pigtail). Photograph the face square-on with the ruler beside it, and once from the side. At the radio opening: is the factory radio plug (G-04) still on the car's loom, how many ways, and is it whole or cut off? The same for the factory amplifier's plug (G-08). On the gauge: the plug on its back that the power lead goes into, whether AEM's own power lead is fitted, and how the two-wire AEMnet lead ends - a small 2-way plug, or bare wires.
DV28 Head unit: the record has, from no source at all - Pioneer DMH-W4660NEX (luxury LP55): the maker's installation sheet was not reached, so the unit's power connector, its ways and whether its power cord is in the box are not known. The devices row assumes a cord with red, yellow, orange, black and blue / white leads, RCA pre-outs and a microphone lead - confirm

expect: Two lines for the plug list, and a word each on G-04 and G-08.

how: Tick V-116 in the app. In the answer type one line per wire: its colour, the car wire it joins, how it is joined, any fuse. Then the list of anything else found, and the two plug lines.
The space left where the radio and the heater controls were. Width side to side, height top to bottom, depth from the front face back to the first thing behind. Smallest of each, in mm.
expect: Three numbers.

how: Behind and below where the glovebox sat: width, height and depth to the firewall or the first thing in the way.
expect: Three numbers.

do: Measure the floor under the dash, driver's side
how: The flat area you could stand a panel on or against: its length and width, and the height from the floor to the first thing above. Note how far the pedals swing.
expect: Length x width, and a height.

do: Measure the floor under the dash, passenger side
how: The same three numbers.
expect: Length x width, and a height.

do: Try the PMU in each space
how: Hold the PMU (131 x 112 x 32.5 mm) where it could mount: low, but more than 50 mm above the footwell floor, its plug facing down or sideways. Check there is room to swing the plug's lever fully.
expect: A yes with the place, or a no with what blocks it.
caution: The PMU is the most expensive part of the build: do not drop it or rest it on a seam that leaks.

how: Where a panel of Deutsch receptacles could face you, measure straight back behind it.
expect: 60 mm or more clear, yes or no.

do: Cut a cardboard pattern of each usable space
how: Trace each space onto cardboard, cut it out and write its name and its depth on it. The node is laid out on these on the bench later.
expect: A labelled pattern for each space.

do: Find where the wideband gauge hides
how: With the gauge still wired, move it to a place behind the dash or in the glovebox region where it is out of sight. Check its sensor lead still reaches the sensor in the exhaust without strain.
expect: A hiding place, and 'lead reaches'.
caution: Do not unplug or stretch the sensor lead.

how: One photo of each with the ruler in shot.
expect: Four or five scaled photos, filed under dash.

how: Open Q-014 and type the centre-stack numbers as the value and the rest in words.
expect: Q-014 answered.

do: Look for the switch on the speedometer head
how: On the back of the cluster, at the speedometer: look for a single extra wire or terminal that is not a lamp. The diagram colours it BR (black, red tracer).
expect: A BR wire or a lone terminal - or nothing.

how: Meter on continuity. One probe on the BR terminal, the other on the cluster's ground (its B wire or metal frame).
expect: Open, or joined, with the speedometer still.

do: Turn the speedometer's input and count
how: With the small screwdriver in the socket where the cable plugs in, turn the input slowly one full turn. Count the beeps.
expect: A whole number of beeps per turn.

how: Turn ten more full turns at a steady pace, counting.
expect: Ten times the first count, none missed.

do: Find where the BR wire ends in the car
how: Behind the dash, follow the BR wire from the speedometer. On the diagram it runs to the cruise control unit's plug, which this car may not have. Label the end SPEED BR and photograph it.
expect: The wire's end labelled, or 'no BR wire in the harness'.

how: Tick Q-115 and type what you found.
expect: Q-115 answered; the agent decides between this switch and the bought sensor.

how: In the app, V-114's answer: the 21 ohm readings and the powered test for each motor.
expect: Both motors' readings in front of you.

how: For each motor: 12 V on R raised the lamp and it stopped by itself; 12 V on RY lowered it and it stopped by itself; YG showed about 12 V only while it moved.
expect: Three yeses per motor, and two currents.

do: Look at each plug and its wires
how: At E-03 (left) and E-04 (right): four wires in the colours WR, YG, R, RY; no splices, no green corrosion in the plug, the boot whole.
expect: Two sound four-way plugs, photographed.

how: Tick V-081 and type the yes / no list and the two currents for each motor.
expect: V-081 answered; the front leg can be pinned.

how: The body side in front of the driver's door, from the sill up. Note what is already there: looms, a bracket, the bonnet release.
expect: A list of what occupies the space.

how: Front to back along the body side, the flat part a panel could sit on. In mm.
expect: A width; the panel wants 150 mm.

how: From 50 mm above the footwell floor up to the first thing that stops a panel.
expect: A height; the panel wants 100 mm.

how: Hold the kick panel back in its place and measure from the body side to the inside face of the trim.
expect: A depth in mm: it has to take a receptacle, its plug and the wires leaving it.

how: Hold the 150 x 100 mm card flat in the space, either way up. Mark its outline with tape where it fits.
expect: It sits flat inside the space - yes or no.

how: On the removed kick panel, measure the diameter of the speaker cut-out in mm.
expect: A diameter for luxury V-103.

how: A photo of the space with the card and the ruler. Then type the value in V-055 and the speaker hole in luxury V-103.
expect: V-055 answered.

how: Inside length, width and depth in mm, at the top and at the floor. Note anything that sticks into it.
expect: Three numbers, with the smaller of each pair.

how: On the battery, measure from the top of the case to the top of a post with its clamp and boot as it will be; if the clamps are not bought yet, measure to the top of the bare post and say so.
expect: A height above the 190 mm case.

how: The battery can stand in for itself, posts taped. Cut cardboard blocks for the disconnect switch, the Class-T fuse block and the amplifier. Their sizes are not in the record: take the switch's and the fuse block's from the makers' drawings, and make the amplifier block the largest that still fits, noting its size.
expect: Three labelled blocks and the battery.
caution: Lithium: a tool across the posts welds. Keep the posts covered.

how: Stand it in the bin where it can be strapped down, long side whichever way leaves the posts to hand.
expect: The battery sitting flat.

do: Place the switch and the fuse block
how: The switch within a few inches of the positive post, where its knob can be turned with the lid open. The Class-T block right beside the switch's output. Then the amplifier beside them.
expect: Everything in the bin, nothing on top of the posts.

how: Imagine the boots on. Put a hand, as if holding a jump lead's clamp, onto each post in turn.
expect: Both posts reached without moving anything.

how: Hold the lid in place over the mock-up.
expect: It closes over the battery and its boots, or it does not - by how many mm.

do: Find the hold-down and ground points
how: Mark where the hold-down would fasten and its backing plate would sit, and where a ground stud could go on bare structural metal near the negative post. Look at what is on the other side of the panel at each point.
expect: The hold-down's place and a stud position, each checked from the other side.
caution: Nothing is drilled today. What lies behind this panel is not in the record: look before any hole is planned.

how: See how the heavy cables would leave the bin toward the tunnel without a sharp bend.
expect: A path noted and photographed.

how: Photos from above and from each side with the ruler in shot; a sketch with the main sizes. Then tick V-088 and type the answers.
expect: V-088 answered.

how: On the removed switch (plug H-13, wires LR and GR): meter across its two terminals.
expect: Open at rest, joined while pressed.

how: The same on plug H-15 (wires LR and GB; two of its four cavities are unused).
expect: Open at rest, joined while pressed.

how: From V-114: did the hatch pop and the fuel door open when each solenoid was fed, and what current did each draw?
expect: Two yes / no answers and two currents.

how: At the hatch solenoid and at the fuel-door solenoid: meter from the solenoid's B wire to bare body metal.
expect: Under 1 ohm at each.

how: At the hatch lock, look for a small switch on the lock body beside the key cylinder with two contact points. Note the colours of its wires and photograph it.
expect: The switch found, its wire colours written down.

how: Meter across the switch's two contacts and work the latch (and the key, if it acts on the switch). Look at its body, its contacts and its wires for the break.
expect: A plain statement: the plastic is cracked, a contact is missing, a wire is off - whatever it is.

how: Photos of the lock, the switch and both solenoids. Tick V-112 and type the answers.
expect: V-112 answered; the agent finishes the release design (A11).

expect: No Blocker or Major open.

how: The Design page in 3D, each leg's pin ladder and route map, the parts list and the cart totals. Stop at anything you could not explain to someone else.
expect: Nothing you do not understand.

expect: Your questions answered.
